title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 26, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: Uh good day out out there today, good week. And you know, as you guys saw, this was first time for our players to go through a regular season schedule. Now, the practice themselves were not how we exactly how we'll do in the regular season, but the schedule was uh so I thought that was good. Running cards for the first time with our players, I think, is good. And you have to be so careful when you're or I should say this, we coached that really, really hard. Having a good card, coaching the guys up so they know what to do and they do it with great effort. What you never want a carded period to do is just turn into a glorified walkthrough. So, I thought our look teams, our scout teams, and our offense and defense going up against those cards did a nice job and room to improve there. But now's the right time to introduce that to our players in terms of how we practice. So, a lot of first this week getting the first time through this schedule, if you will, and I thought the guys handled it well. And next thing we'll do is we'll have a walk through tomorrow morning uh before we get on the airplane and head down to Miami. uh pleased with where uh where where we are from a work progress standpoint and the guys process I guess I should say I'm pleased with the process and now um we got a game Friday night. >> How' Mike look to you this week? >> I thought he did did well and I think you guys are getting a chance to talk to him and uh I don't want to put words in Mike's mouth but I thought he he looked good. He uh moved around well. Um, I think all that work, like I've told you guys the whole time and you've seen it with your own eyes, like he's put a lot of work into this and I I think you see uh I think you see that in in his, you know, getting away from center, making throws, etc., etc. >> Will he play this week? >> Mike will not play. >> How do you plan to kind of handle the snap count at quarterback? >> Uh, two starts. Coupe goes in next, Jack goes in next. Kevin, when you guys uh start making the final decision on who's going to start, how much will Matt Ryan's uh input factor into the final decision? >> Yeah. You know, Matt's input factors into every decision that that I make and that Ian makes. I mean, we talk through these things. You know, these are uh I don't care what no matter how big or small the decision, we talk about it. And that's uh you know, that's myself, that's Matt, that's Ian, that's Greg Beatles. You know, we say if we're gonna be accused of anything, you want to be accused of overcommunicating on all things. So, uh, certainly Matt's input will be taken into account on on all roster decisions. Um, because he he Matt's a very good listener. So, I think he's he's does a great job of, uh, listening and and hearing and if he wants to provide his own thoughts, he he does and will, but, um, he's a, you know, big factor in really everything we do. >> Also, how much will you guys look at what these guys have done in the past as NFL quarterbacks as opposed to right now? Is that a big factor, particularly last year? Yeah, I think with any evaluation really at any position, I think you do have to look at a body of work in their past. Obviously, I can only speak to the time I've been with players and live, if you will, uh, coaching guys, but certainly you do look at at your past and see what players have done in the course of their career. Certainly, >> with PennX not playing Friday, is is there still the potential that he could play once you get to the reg? >> I'm not going to get into week one. Obviously, uh, we're I'm best served and we're best served by keeping it dayto-day and and focusing on what's in front of us. Um, really this was an important week for Mike. First time out there with people around you, the offensive line, the defensive line. And I think, uh, going through a a a drill where you got to move up in the pocket or get chased out of the pocket, whatever it is. So, uh, I thought a really good first step for Mike in that regard. But, uh, outside of this week, I don't think it's fair to to go farther than that. >> Any other starters you plan on holding out of that game? Uh, >> no. What's the rep count going to look like? Are you wanting to give the starters more of a a load in this game compared to that first game? >> Yeah, you know, spent a lot of time thinking about this. And one of the things that you learn uh from the data that medical provides you is how much you should do h what playing in these games, what playing in joint practices does to your first few weeks of the season from a soft tissue perspective, which I believe in. just great data that is shared with us at the league meetings and um we've tried to follow through on a lot of that. So getting x number of plays in in preeason, getting two joint practices I I think sets you up for success in the fall. It's not a guarantee of anything, but uh it does set you up. So we have a plan. Uh we'll see how many plays we get. I also know I want to get down there and see what the game looks like and how the guys are doing and that type of thing. But um starters will play. Um there are play time will vary by person. Um in terms of what we end up doing with each player. >> What do you want to see from Zulo on Friday? >> Same as every quarterback. You know, in any game you go out there, just operate, you know, take what's there, get us in and out of plays, those type of things. >> The soft tissue data, is it a matter of not getting them too many snaps or getting them enough snaps? >> I think enough. I think enough. I I think there's a a sweet spot there. Again, it's u it's not 100% like like anything. Um but I do think there's something to be said for we use the word callous, but getting your bodies ready for a season and not o and not overdoing it either. Um, you know, not that I've been doing this forever, but back when it was four preseason games, it was always, you know, 10 plays in the first game, first quarter, and the second game, uh, you know, into the second quarter, maybe get a two-minute drive at the and then come out of the halftime in the third game. So, you'd play the first half, and you'd come out of the halftime and put a drive together in the third game, and then you wouldn't play in the fourth game. So, uh, that's how everybody always did it and and it's changed and I know the number of preseason games has changed as well. Um, I don't know that there's right one right way or wrong way, but I I do trust in having all this data available to us and and make sure that we put our guys in position to be set up for success week one through week 17 and so on if you earn the plus part of that. So, uh, just tried to be very intentional about how you put the training camp together, the preseason plan together, all in an effort to get ready for what is, as we all know, a long season. >> When would you want to name a starter for IQB? >> Uh, whenever they tell me I have to when that depth chart has to be put out. >> No. Yeah. Not I'm not honestly not trying to be Cy. Just uh we'll focus on what's available to us, what information is available to us. Obviously, uh, this has been something that, you know, we need to work through as as people come back off of injury. I mean, Tua was injured to start camp and then Mike's been injured, you know, and not doing the 11 on 111. So, you just every day you're just trying to make decisions based on who's available to you. The good news is, uh, very, very happy with our guys and the progress they've all made. >> I mean, ideally before week one, the start of week one, the end of week, like before the game. >> Yeah. I not, you know, I'm truly not trying to be koi. I just I know it's not today. Uh so I think we'll we'll worry about this week and then circle back with you guys next week. >> AP had mentioned back in in May that ideally you'd want your guy named by the end of camp. >> Are you worried that you haven't gotten to that point yet? >> When does camp end? >> I believe this is the last practice of camp, I believe. >> Is it? >> Believe so. >> Yeah. It's funny. Somebody's like, "When do you break camp?" I'm like, "I don't know." You know, to me it's training camp until week one rolls around. So, uh, I think ideally at every single position, you'd love to to have starters that are returning, 22 out of 22, but we'll just worry about what's in front of us and, um, we'll take all the information we have available to us and then make the decision when when appropriate when really when we have to. >> Jawan Taylor and Jake Matthews rest days. >> Yes. >> Uh, with Mike just not playing in Friday's game, is that just kind of part of a his acclamation still? >> Exactly. Yeah, just got back to team drills on Monday. So, just felt to keep the focus on on these three days and see how I came out of it and and again, you guys can talk to him, but I think he did well. >> Kevin, going back to the uh directly in the back, going back to the first preseason game afterwards, Tua says he wasn't happy about the operational stuff on his end of the offense. What have you seen from him and his command since that point? Yeah, I I think doing a doing a good job and and that's something uh all of our players are really on offense playing in a new system and and getting all these reps and getting the walkthrough reps and making sure that we're all on on point, if you will. Uh and there's there's something to be said in in football where you make a mistake and then our job as coaches is to identify and correct. So, when something is wrong on the football field, we hustle in here, we watch the tape, and we get it fixed. And uh there's things from those plays in the Denver game that we learned from, we corrected. Uh so I think all of our players, too included, uh takes all of that coaching to heart and and tries to be one day better uh after it. >> I know we're nowhere close to naming a starter. It's not that point for you. But when you do name it, is it the idea of this is the guy for the whole season or do you have a, you know, do you operate in terms of two guys of equality to have a shorter leash? How do you go about? Yeah, honestly not really focused on on much past Miami at this point. Um, but we'll deal with that when we get to it. >> Anything else? >> Oh, did want to ask one more. Uh, guy you coached, Nick Chup, uh, >> Georgia Bulldog. >> Yeah. Uh, you coached him for a while now. It's his retirement. You know, what can you say about him, the player and the person, you know, getting to coach him? >> Yeah. Special person. Uh, really special player. Uh, you know, I don't have a vote for Hall of Famers, but Hall of Fame person, Hall of Fame player in my my book. Um, fun fun to coach, not hard to coach, just easy to coach. Uh, always did everything the right way. Not a very loud person, but man, there's such power in leading by example and always doing the right thing. And then just the the way in which he ran the football and how physical he was with that breakaway speed. uh I was had a front row seat to some incredible individual efforts and I I say individual now great blocking and that type of thing but just the the way he was able to break through tackles and uh some some amazing moments that I I was lucky and blessed and fortunate to be a part of. >> I have one quick Kevin in the in your past have you preferred your starting quarterbacks to play in the preseason games or is that is it that big of a deal? >> It's it really depends on the player. Uh, honestly, it depends on the player, depends on the offense, what you need to accomplish. I really think the preseason, those type of decisions, uh, in terms of who plays, when they play, how long they play. I I I think you have to take that week, year to year because the it depends on what the player needs in that given year. Depend depends on what your team needs in in that given year. So, u really does vary by by person. Thank you. >> Okay. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it. Thank you.

title: Caleb Williams encourages offense to celebrate big plays | Press Conference
text: That's not >> Whatever coach, yeah, whatever coach says. >> Anything else you want to pre-empt >> No, no, that's it. That's it. Good day. Good day. Uh a lot of learning. Um you know, at the end got to got to trust coach right there. Um I kind of um was was pushing for a play and we were in a a weird yardage and um just trusting coach and um you know, allow him to you know, be the the the magician of a play caller he is. >> What do you mean by that? >> Yeah, I I was pushing for a specific play. Just, you know, trying to feel it and um trying to trying to get a match-up and we were super far out compared to the play and um just just just trusting him uh on on you know, he's done it for he's done it for a while now. So, uh just just being able to trust him with the play call and um you know, go through the right reads and you know, get the ball to right spot. >> Were you going for Colson there? >> I was going for Colson, yeah. >> Caleb, it seemed like you got off to a a pretty hot start. Like what was working for you guys early on in the >> Yeah, it's just uh something that I would say from last week to to this week is just working on execution. Um the flags and things like that. Um and then and then also like uh I said it's it's it's leading from the head of the snake uh down to the tail and you know, when we come out with good energy when we come out and we're executing, when we come out we're not having penalties and things like that as as first team, um it trickles down um you know, to the second team and third team and just having that energy. And so, uh being able to start like that we got to we got to be able to start like that throughout the year and then uh you know, when we when we come out from half time, we got to come out better than I would say than we did today. >> What do you think was your best play of the day today? >> Um I have no idea. Yeah, I have no I uh I'm blanking. I threw a I threw a good ball to uh I think it was Rome. Um you know, middle of the field over there on a crosser. Uh that that he you know, he was able to turn up field and and and have a run with the ball. So, I'd say that one for right now. >> Was it Was it just Swift on the toss back to you for the throw to >> Uh that was a pretty good toss, too. Uh yeah. Yeah, Swift uh threw it back to me. It was a double pass. Swift threw it back to me. Um, tight end Colston and and Rome did a good job. I believe it was Rome over there on the left side at X. Uh, he did a good job uh, just just being really patient, letting the, you know, letting the play develop and happen and then just shooting down the field, taking the deep coverage out. And Colston lost his guy, so it was it was really cool. >> Did they say anything about a trick play in practice? >> Uh, who? Titans? Uh, no, if they did, I didn't hear them. Yeah. >> Hey, well, how did you feel about the red zone work overall today? >> Um, how much red zone work did we get today? >> Early on. Early on. >> It wasn't it wasn't much. Uh, felt solid. I I think uh, was that 7 on? I'm I'm I'm blanking on on on the day, sorry. Um, 7 on. I I missed the pass that I should have hit early on, the first first or second pass and then uh, I think I only had three reps or so and so I think the other two we hit and so um, obviously you want to go three for three. I would say 7 on especially is is is a offensive advantage play uh, or or situation and so uh, just trying to be as consistent as possible. >> I mean, red zone's been pretty good. Um, where do you feel like you've gotten better at processing? >> Yeah. Uh, I wouldn't say it's processing. I think it's just I think it's just understanding the play better or the plays that that we've put in. Um, and then not having to necessarily, you know, relearn plays and things like that or or or, you know, just learn plays overall. Um, and and coach can add in more detail, coach can add in more uh, more plays and and so um, it's been fun, it's been exciting and then uh, you know, just just my feet I would say has been the biggest thing down here, just being able to be in in rhythm and and smooth and delivering the guys a good ball. >> Do you have confidence in the left tackle situation right now? >> Yeah. I uh, I didn't I mean, other than that one period where it wasn't just the left tackle, we had the guys coming, you know, down the middle, right side, left side and so um, you know, I I I feel good. I've I've played with both those guys out there um, between Braxton and and Theo and so we got live reps, we got real reps, we got game reps, we got practice reps over the past, I guess I mean it's 3 years now for me. Um going into my third year and so um yeah, I feel I feel good with with uh where those guys are at and and whatever co- uh decision coach makes. >> Well, Ben Ben's been pushing recently for the next jump from you and your coach recognition. How do you describe what is next for you in that regard? >> Yeah, it's just you know, at times you have you have five guys going out in a in a um in a in a concept. And so portions of the concepts are specific certain uh certain coverages or certain looks and so uh just just not necessarily going 1 2 3 4 5. It's it's okay, we can we can skip this route because of this coverage or the you know, this post high or you know, they're split split field and and things like that. And so um you know, it's just being able to process those things faster and it's it's just been like I said like I said, it's it's just been faster or or more comfortable with the plays and being able to uh not necessarily think about the plays anymore. You know, I'm I'm I'm more or less getting up there and trying to figure out uh you know, what I can fix uh to make sure this play works or make sure this you know, this um this drive works. And so um you know, there's times where we may have the coverage and something happens and it's been able to adjust and find a check down and scramble and and and be positive in in those ways. >> How do you learn to process that faster? Is it just as simple as reps? >> Oh man, it's reps. It's reps and it's not just it's not on the grass and between the 120 and 53. It's it's being able to consistently I mean, I write the same like if it's a common concept, you know, that that everybody runs in the NFL. I write it down consistently. I write down the uh you know, what we like it verse, what we don't like it verse um every time that the play is put in and installed. And so it's just I'm getting constant mental reps of of you know, when I see a coverage or when I see this, it's it's okay, we don't like it verse this. Now, let's get on to the the back side of the concept or you know, another route that you know, uh that we that we do like in that concept. >> And I think John Elway said the other day that he told the team he want the offense celebrating when the team gets in the end zone. Why is that message important to you? >> Yeah, uh one it's I mean it's it's really freaking hard to score in NFL. When you get into games and things like that it's it's really freaking hard. And so let's I mean let's let's go celebrate when we do it. Two it it shows a sense of love and care for your teammates. Um because you didn't get in the end zone. You know, you you weren't the one getting in the end zone so you got to go down there and celebrate and have fun and dance and do all these things and you know, come back to the sideline, focus up and you know, get ready to go do it again. So it's it's something like the the Spurs Tony Parker a couple years ago. It's like you know, um if it was this this stat of like they go around and they they slap hands more than anybody and it's it's those small things, those small connections, those small moments that that build up and you know, when it when it comes down to it in those big moments something from those moments and slapping hands and going down and and celebrating with your teammates they they show up late in games, late in the year and things like that. And so um it's important it's and it's uh it's really important to me and us. >> A couple more here? >> Are you seeing any small ways in which Ben is coaching the team differently this year versus last year? >> Uh I would say I would say he's he's still extremely sharp. Uh and and and uh you know, on us you know, very very tough. Um and I think he's I would say he may have less moments where he's consistently more angry but when he does he you know, he's he's he's really on he's really on us and and things like that and uh it just shows how much he cares for us. And then I think another piece of it is is is allowing us, you know, we got a a bunch of guys that are coming back and have came back that um know the offense and know what it looks like and I think Ben's allowing us to be able to like today I got I got angry on the field and Ben's like calm down. You know, typically it's you know, it's been Ben you know, last year um and it's I think he's allowing us players to be able to step up and I think uh I think I said this last year or the year before maybe early this year is that players uh you know, you win championships um you know, when you're when you're a player led team. And so I think coach is trying to allow us to do that and he He in whenever he needs to cuz that's that's his position and and he has the right to do so. And so, um but I will say he he is allowing us to step up as as players to lead us. >> Caleb, if you could just shift back to to last year, what really clicked with you going from a rookie to a second-year quarterback? And what's some advice that you would give to Cam Ward who's doing the same thing this year? >> Yeah, I think I think he has a awesome coordinator that's that's been uh in the league for I mean, he's been in the league for a while now. I don't know I don't know how long, but he's been in the league and he's been he's been a um awesome offensive coordinator and things like that and he's been in different places with different quarterbacks. So, he has a um yeah, and he has a good track record with quarterbacks and things like that and some quarterbacks that he's been with. And so, um just believing and trusting in him um and and what he's coaching you and teaching you and then um you know, I think I think just being able to go out there and execute. And um I think I I we have some similarities in our game and and things like that. I've been able to make, you know, the big plays and things like that and and and just being able to keep consistently making the small plays. And I'm still working on my stuff. So, I can't I can't speak on it too much and you know, and and and things like that. But I I yeah, I would say those are the the few things. >> Dan, last one. >> Caleb, you made a couple of decisions offensively in the spring that to get a little bit more out of scramble drill. What have you seen over the last 5 months that encourages you about what you're >> Yeah, we've been we've had the uh we've I would say we've been getting better. We work on it uh once or twice each week and then obviously as a drill and then obviously we have um them happen in in in joint practices or just practices and you know, um scrimmages or whatever the case may be. And so, it's just been able to uh refine them. It's it's another play um in itself. And so, we coach it that way. Uh we preach it that way. We look after it that way and uh we believe in it that way. And so, I think we're going to keep growing. I think it's a it's a it's a piece of our offense that's going to be big for us. It's a piece of piece of our offense that uh will help make us one of the most explosive and not the most explosive uh offense in the league is what we're you know, we're searching for uh cuz that's our part. And so, uh that's our part to Chicago Bears, our part to you defense and special teams. And so, uh we're going to keep striving for greatness. We're going to keep striving to um perfect what we need to perfect in those ways. Um and then, uh you we're going to try and stay out of scrambles as much as possible. When it does happen, uh we're going to try and light up and be explosive. >> Okay.

title: Grady Jarrett on joint practices: 'It's always fun' | Press Conference
text: Can't finish training camp without a good burner. So, today we had one. It was fun to come out here and compete against them, man. It was awesome day. So, uh feel good and uh excited to, you know, um get to the end of the preseason and get ready into the um but we got to finish our game, obviously, and um you know, just continue to build. >> What are you feeling like you've squeezed out of these two joint practices the last two weeks? >> Uh I think just seeing where we at as a team, uh being able to compete against uh other pe- other people's always fun. And uh we don't have to beat up beat up on each other all the time. So, to go against, you know, two teams the last two weeks that's that's really well, really physical. I think we did a really good job and it was good to get the work and we definitely appreciate it. >> Grady, you had a pretty big hit in practice today. How do you balance that physicality but also like >> You know, uh some- We we practice a certain way. Um we got, you know, way we want to play ball and uh nothing is done with malice, but we got to play our style of defense the way we want to at all times. And um and you know, sometimes things happen and I mean, you know, just one of those things that happen, but you know, it is what it it kind of is what it is, you know. >> It It looked like early on you guys really wanted to set the tempo with that that play style. Was that kind of the messaging going over there? >> I mean, I would I would I would just say every time we take the field is the style of defense we want to play. Um and um I think we did that early. I think our key now is to sustain that through the um whole through the whole outing, whether it's the whole game. Feel like after halftime, you know, we had to revamp it back up, but we got to find a way to continue to challenge ourselves to keep that physical, that aggressiveness all the way through the end of the game. And then that's how I think we take the next step, but I mean, we we we want to play our style of defense anytime we have the opportunity to and um and I think we I think we did well. >> Grady, uh the coaches talked about the uh interior depth being a a plus this year. Who have you seen make the most of uh that opportunity from your view? >> I think it's been a collective effort. Like I said back in the spring, um it was just getting back to the basics of the style we want to play, the way you want to be in our stance, the way you want to strike off the ball. And I think everybody is helping everybody across the board. And um and I just think it's been a collective group effort from the coaches challenges every day, players buying in and coming out here executing on the field and I think everybody reaping the benefits right now from the time that we put in in the off season through training camp and we'll continue to as we continue to focus on our fundamentals and try to get better. >> Do you find that Vandenburg kind of has your ear a lot asking you a lot of questions? >> Um I mean I think it's been an obviously it was you know that's the part that seen a lot but it's a lot of work put in with all the guys man from the rookies to the vets. We have a really really healthy connection in our room. We work hand in hand. We talk to the rooks, the rooks talk to us and it's been awesome to have that just that that that feeling in the room with between the coaches and the players that we can have trust with each other and we all speak in one language on what's expected so if he come to me or if I go to somebody else or somebody else go to somebody else we all speaking the same language. It's just little reminders and that's that's been a super fun part of this year having a really close knit group of insiders and and as far as the ends as well. So we all speaking the same language and that's how we can communicate so well across the board. >> Between that between the heat and the and how deep into training camp you guys are now is this the most intense practice you guys have had? >> I mean I I don't know if I'll say most intense. I think it was just the next practice up you know at the end of the day any anybody anywhere anytime we got to do what we do the job got to get done and and uh I don't even think we looking at it like that. We just want to win each day do our best and let the rest take care of it so >> What >> You got something? >> Yeah I just want to know what you thought of having a half time. I don't know if that's something you had I haven't seen that >> I've I've I've had it in the past before. We we don't usually do that in the way we practice at at home but it was good. It was good simulation for actual game time because you going to come out hot and there's going to be a half time in the game you got to be able to maintain that and that's a growing lesson for us and so I mean it is what it is however they want to do it we'll we'll be ready to go. >> Last two, Phil and Adam. How do you feel with your mom starring in a commercial now? >> Oh, mama been doing that years and years. Go back and do your research, baby. We been doing working with product game for a long time since I was with Atlanta. Uh, she just had a she had the opportunity to do the do the the last shoot. It was awesome. Um, she had so much fun. They shot up in Vancouver. So, to be able to um, you know, her just continue to the I mean, look, mama living the dream, you feel me? You know? So, I'm I'm excited. I'm excited for her to continue to, you know, um, just I mean, do her thing. And I She always representing and uh, and I'm proud of her and I mean, it's just awesome to see um, her do it in the Chicago Bears jersey now and that's awesome. And so, we we love it and people been showing her a lot of love. But, however we can do to, you know, bring a positive impact to the team where the city wherever we at, um, we always trying to do that. >> You said you wanted to win the day. Did you feel like you guys won the day? >> I mean, I feel like we definitely came out put put put put a really put a really good effort forward today. Uh, we do got to go and review the review the tape. But, I think the attack mindset was there. And um, there's a lot to learn from. I think our finish could be better as a whole unit. Um, but that's just was a challenge of what come with training camp at the end of it. You know, hot challenging day, which is no excuse, but is also a growth opportunity for us. And um, but it definitely was a successful productive day and I'm proud of the whole team, not even the defense, not just the defense.

title: Ben Johnson: 'Does it help us win or not?' | Press Conference

title: Browns vs. Patriots Postgame Recap | Cleveland Browns
text: Nathan Zegura here at Huntington Bank Field where the Browns close out the preseason in style with a 37-13 win over the defending AFC champion New England Patriots. Now, of course, the starters for the Browns and the starters for the Patriots did not play in this one, but this is real-life drama. This is reality TV. People playing for their roles, people playing for their football livelihoods, trying to make the Browns 53-man roster or at least show enough to make a 53-man roster elsewhere if it doesn't work out here in Cleveland. Now, those cutdowns will come on Sunday where they've got to get this roster from 90 down to 53. For the Browns today, this was a fun one. The offense absolutely humming. They put up 27 points in the first half led by Dylan Gabriel who had the best performance he's had in a Cleveland Browns uniform. He went 12 of 15, 180 yards, three touchdowns. Basically, a perfect quarterback rating. 158.3 is perfect. He was 157.9. In complete command. Looked great off of play-action. Looked great in the drop-back game, even in the read-option game. And he would just lead this team up and down the field. Now, his first two touchdowns, Luke Fouria! Fouria! He just continues to do it. He had a third touchdown that was called back. The ball just touched the ground, but Luke Fouria now, two games here, scores three times. He has the big catch in Chicago making an absolute push to make this roster, the local kid from Mentor, to make this roster here on the Cleveland Browns. That was fun to watch. The young running backs, Rocket Sanders, had a great day running the football. Armani Marshall caught a touchdown pass from Dylan Gabriel. Davion Booth had 40 yards, was hitting spin moves like it was Madden en route to his touchdown. The Browns even had a guy named Ben Patterson have two catches lead the team in receiving over 70 yards from the University of Texas, Permian Basin. What? Where is that from? Permian Basin. I even misspelled it. It's only the second player ever from that school to be on an NFL roster. At 6'5, he stood out today. The Browns just had it all working. All the young guys, the lines were good, controlled the line of scrimmage with the second team, with the third team. It was just fun to watch. And then speaking of fun to watch, Taylen Green comes in in the second half, at one point leads a 98-yard touchdown drive. He had a play that you got to go seek the highlight out of. Looked like he was going to run himself into a safety. The next thing you know, he's sprinting down the field for 30 yards. In fact, he would be the team's leading rusher. In fact, he'd be the game's leading rusher here. Eight carries, 66 yards in this one for Taylen Green. Also completed five of his seven passes. He is fun. I think there is a world in which you can have him in certain packages in the red zone because he changes the numbers in the run game. He now turns it from 10 on 11 to 11 on 11 or even 11 on 10 in those read options. And when he makes those defensive ends play flat-footed because they respect his speed. So, that was great to watch. All in all, great performance on the offense. Andre Smith made all seven of his kicks, three for three on field goals, four for four on extra points. Long field goal today of 47 yards. Heck, even Corey Bojorquez hit a beautiful 55-yarder to the sideline. Defensively, the young guys showing up again. Justin Jefferson, your fifth-round draft pick this year out of Alabama, team-high nine tackles. He gets a sack. He gets an interception. Logan Fano knocking that one in the air as he hit the quarterback. Jefferson picking it off. Easton Mascarenas-Arnold had an interception. Donovan Peoples-Jones had an interception. And yes, I give it to him even though they called pass interference. There was no pass interference. That was an interception. Cordell Wilson trying to make this team a defensive end, had a sack, his second of the preseason. Aidan Huntington was all over the field. This was just a fun game to watch. Fun game to be a part of for the Cleveland Browns and a fun way to end this preseason getting Todd Monken his first win as the Cleveland Browns head coach. And I know it's only a preseason win. Now the real test will come to get that first win down in Jacksonville in just 17 days. All eyes though on this Sunday, that's when every roster around the NFL must be trimmed down to 53. Tough decisions remain for this Cleveland Browns team. Do they keep all four quarterbacks? Who's the fifth or sixth receiver? I think fifth is Jaelon Darden. So, who's the sixth receiver? Did Luke Floria do enough? I don't know how much more he could have done. He's looked great. Defensive end, corner, linebacker, safety, lot of places, tight end, lot of decisions going to have to be made here for general manager Andrew Berry to get this roster down to the initial 53. Remember, it's just the initial, then the cuts happen around the league, you have a chance to claim guys off of waivers, and then kind of get to your set 53s you get ready to roll into the season, and then set your practice squad of 16 guys on top of that. So, good end here, 37 to 13 win, a lot of young guys making contributions here. It was fun to watch Dillon Gabriel put on a show, Taylen Green put on a show. The Browns, four quarterbacks, we have not seen that in quite some time. We could see that this year. ClevelandBrowns.com, the Browns Mobile App, we're going to have all of this covered for you on the cut down to 53. So, keep your eyes out for that. And man, fun way to end it here at Huntington Bank Field. Next stop, Jacksonville. This has been your game recap, the Browns closing out the preseason in style.

Like Josh Dobbs has shown some things on the practice field where like I totally get it. I do. I get what they see in him. I think he's a perfect backup. >> Yeah, and he's shown enough things over the course of his career that of those two, he would be more likely to be claimed if they cut him. And honestly, that's what a lot of these decisions have to come down to. Like which player can can we can we afford to lose last and who's more likely to be claimed if we expose him. And the answer just based on his experience is Dobbs. And so that, you know, that probably has has to be the the biggest factor taken into consideration here. It's not even a conversation about like who is the better quarterback right now. It's as Justin said, who is best fit to serve as as Jared's support man. And I think to us anyways, that's pretty clearly Josh Dobbs. >> Hey guys, Jeff here. I appreciate you for watching the clip, but subscribe and like the video to never miss out on future uploads. And don't forget, go Lions.

title: Colts players on injury returns, position rotations
text: How good was it to get back out there? >> It was good. It was good, you know. Missed it. >> What kind of reception did you get from the guys? It seemed like they were eager to get you back. >> Yeah, yeah. No, it was it was it was fun to be back out here, you know. A lot of guys were happy to see me. Uh I I kind of kind of snuck my way back in there. So, got a lot of guys that just like were noticing me in stretch lines and stuff. So, it was fun. >> How did it feel and what are some things that you feel that you've got to fine-tune before it's full systems go? >> Yeah, you know, just first time being back out here. Um wearing the helmet, you know, playing with the other NFL players, right? So, it's it's you got to knock a little bit of rust off, but um been working in PT, been working kind of off and on with the trainers. They've been doing a good job preparing me, getting me ready. Um so, you know, just just a little different once you get it back out here, you know, get timing from from Daniel and these other NFL arms. So, >> I know I know the coach do behind the scenes with the trainers. How long have you been really ramped up? >> All through off this time. >> Yeah, I've been ramping up um all throughout camp. So, it's really since, you know, when we reported like end of July. >> We always want to know are you ahead of schedule, behind schedule? Or are you on your schedule? >> I'm on my schedule. Well, where where where where we want to be. >> I I know coach, I know >> you expect to be ready for week one and also just mentally how did you just get through the last few months of not playing football? >> Yeah, that week one is the goal and um you know, mentally like it it is tough. You guys just got to find ways to try and stay stay in it, you know, cuz you're going to be in those meetings and stuff and as as it's good to be around the guys. They kind of they keep your spirits up and stuff cuz, you know, sitting in in watching film and and watching walk-through, watching practice like it gets it gets a little monotonous. You want to be out there. You want to be out there, you know, helping the team, making plays with the team, you know, work working with your brothers, you know. So, um but the guys have been great. They've been checking in with me, you know. Just ev- other than just not being out there on the field, everything's been the same. >> I know you've been watching from afar on the sidelines, but how did it feel to actually be out there with all the talent around you? Talk about DJ, you talk about your wide receivers. >> Yeah, no, it felt great, you know, it's it's good. It's good to be able to finally join the field with with Keenan, you know, excited we have him. Um he's a guy you can can learn so much from. Um you know, DJ, getting back out there, working some time in. yeah, it's it's it's great. It's it's That's what That's what I want to do. I want to be out here. That's the fun part about it. Just getting to play football. >> You You mentioned Keenan and we were talking to Mo Alie-Cox a few others and they were saying he's often your teach tape in film. So, what is it like to have that in person and how do you think he can help your game? >> Yeah, it's super special. I just like picking up little things. One, I mean, I see the way he he prepares, the way he like watches film and kind of studies the game. Uh that's something I'm trying to pick his brain on and learn from a little bit. And then two, just like like watching little moves. It can be it keeps constantly working on things. Walk-through, you know, he's throwing little moves out there and stuff. So, I think I'm kind of like learning and you just always watch that and try to pick up pick up stuff from his game, steal from his game a little bit. >> What about conditioning-wise, how do you feel? Cuz I mean, it's a lower body injury, so you know, I'm sure you have to you know, limit yourself to some degree. So, how how do you feel that way? >> Yeah, I feel good. That That's been the whole thing with this um this past month is is really ramping up and kind of building that stamina back up. Um and more so I'd say even like like leg like not like cardio stamina, but like leg-wise stamina, you know, so just getting back to it. Uh they they do a great job in the training room and the sports science, you know, having say, "Hey, we want you to hit these numbers today. Um last week we did this. This week, you know, we want to get 20% more or whatever it is." So, leave that to them. I trust in them and from how I'm feeling, I can tell it's it's they're they're doing their job and they're doing well. >> Is this the longest absence you've had? I don't know why I can't remember your injury history off the top of my >> Uh yeah, this is the longest I've been out, for sure. >> And and so, that was new for you, right? So, how did you What did you find direct What did you learn about having to be away from football for so >> Yeah, um you know, it may it makes you being out and watching and standing on the sideline makes you appreciate the appreciate the game, appreciate the the grind that is practice, appreciate all that because you know, especially like times like this it's tough it's tough to practice and it's hot and sometimes it can be a little bit miserable out there feeling, but um you know, being on the sideline makes you makes you miss it, makes you makes you want to be out there, you know, and then just be with your your teammates, your brothers. >> Given that situation, what are like is it is it speed? Is it strength? Is it quickness? Like what are the things that you feel like are separating you from being like what you would say is 100% um and and what you're trying to work on in the next couple of weeks? >> Yeah, I would I would say all those. >> Yeah. >> Given your chance to look at the team, uh where do you think they are and how do you think you can help them? >> Uh I think that I think they're looking good, you know, I I I think I reflect back to to last year and just knowing like um we didn't probably know where our our quarterback our starting quarterback till around this time. So, um or maybe a week or two prior, so I think the amount of reps like we've got at camp and the the chemistry we've built, even though like we just added Keenan, I I know he's he's a guy that just being such a vet, I think he can click in and like him and Daniel build chemistry fast, I would expect. Um but then other than that just like Daniel being in the huddle, you know, working with the guys. We got a lot of guys who might have been their first start like I on the line like last year I think a lot of guys was their first year. This year I think they're most of them are back. I know like guys Jaylen's probably the only new starter, but he he got a decent amount of experience last year. Um so yeah, I think it's I think we're definitely, you know, in terms of like being together and being on the team, I think we're probably ahead of what we were last year, so I think that's a good sign. >> Given that chemistry and that connection that you have with Daniel, how confident are you where you guys can pick up right where you've left off? >> Yeah, um confident, you know, I think I think we we continued to get better every game we had last year and I think we if you kind of look at it like as a season from the start of the season to like week eight of the season like if you just looked every week I think we were getting better chemistry and better on the same page so I don't think anything has changed in that. I think we're going to pick off where we left off last year and continue to like keep building that. >> You walked us through it here Nathan. You walked us through it a little bit when we talked in June. Um just about the whole process of going with the PRP shot a couple days after the season ended and then having to wait eight weeks going um getting surgery in late March. Was the the choice to avoid surgery until March just because as an athlete you want to avoid that whenever possible or I guess kind of in hindsight can you reflect or can you kind of take us through the thought process and and what these last six months have been like? >> Yeah, I think um I'm definitely with the mindset of like trying to avoid avoid the knife as much as possible, you know, like I think you can do a lot with with PT and rehab and um you know, so that's what we did. We we did that shot and I I started a bunch of PT and and rehab and we scanned to see if if the issue had been solved and it hadn't been solved and then we found out kind of had something bone wise that was causing the issue so just went and went ahead and kind of you know, got rid of the issue so didn't continue to hurt myself. >> And then when this rehab process is all said and done is the expectation that you'll be back 100% the exact same guy that you were before this? >> Yes. >> I guess so overall generally this week do you like how you guys were able to get back and uh kind of get back to the standard that kind of lacked last Saturday? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean it's always good to come back out and continue working on the things that you need to like get better at, prepare for and being back here it's always also nice. I mean being back where you're covered I mean where you're normally at so get back to work. >> You worked a lot at center uh second team center throughout the summer. How do you think that move has has gone for you? >> Um I think it's been great. I mean, I've been having a lot of fun in there. I mean, a lot of support from the guys in the room, Coach Tony, Watt, really everybody. Um it's another challenge. I mean, I've been enjoying the challenge of learning a new spot and really challenging myself to get everything that I need to do there and also I'm about to guard if I need to as well. >> What are some of the challenges of making sure you're as sharp as possible at center, but knowing that okay, I still need to make sure I can do the guard stuff as well? >> I mean, obviously making the IDs, communicating with everybody in the O-line, tight ends, running backs, QBs. big part is communication and just making the IDs and always make sure you get the snap back there and your technique is as good as you want it to be and good as it needs to be. >> You not only have to adapt between spots, but you're adapting for a rotation of different quarterbacks over the course of camp. How have you been able to navigate that with the three different guys? >> Yeah, I mean, I think the the QB room does really good of trying to to get everything like in sync of how they're doing it, how they're communicating, their cadences. Um I feel like they've been doing a really good job with that and really helping us out, especially me being a new center. I mean, it really helps out, so. >> What are your goals for the last game for you guys? What what are some things you're looking to get out of this last preseason game? >> Uh really just go out there and everyone go play go play go uh make some plays, keep working on the things that we need to have been working on for the past preseason and just go out there and compete and just have fun together. >> What things have been >> shotgun snap, just doing it over and over again. >> Um first time doing it it's pretty difficult, but once you keep doing it and just doing the repetitions over and over again, um just got to find that spot and send it back there with with confidence, so. >> Was it something you'd never done before? >> No, I haven't. So, that's that's why it's been so fun, just learning something new, so. >> What's been most beneficial having Tanner there working alongside him? >> Oh, he's been in my pocket the whole time. Like telling me what how he sees stuff. Um how he's like his how he snaps it and just how he sees the line. He's telling me to study. Um it's been really big. Everyone in the whole O-line has been a really big help. >> Thanks, Dalton. From the start of camp to now going into the final preseason game, what are the greatest strides that you have seen with this defense? >> Uh I think this communicate the communicate his standpoint. Like it was a lot of new pieces and a lot of new faces from the rookie from the free agents. Um so, this again like that togetherness from the communication standpoint and these guys like trusting each other, trusting uh the calls they getting the checks and all that stuff and just getting lined up being able to play fast. >> How significant has that communication, getting on the same page with Cam, been? >> I think it's easy cuz I mean Cam is a smart player. So, I mean it's he learned the defense pretty quick uh last year. So, it's just refreshes for him. So, I mean it's easy to communicate with him and I mean he understands the defense. Uh a bunch of guys on the standard. So, I mean really it's easy with him. >> What are the team's goals for the third >> Uh tomorrow from like the the first group or just all as a whole? >> Just as a whole. >> As a whole, I mean definitely not putting what we put on the tape last week. >> [laughter] >> Uh going out there dominating it. Whoever is on the field is dominating. Uh playing fast and just setting the standard for uh for this defense what we're going to be about and just running hitting and just uh playing fast and having fun. >> We've seen you and uh Jaylon Carlile has taken a lot of the first team reps at linebacker over the last week or two. What is your the chemistry and relationship like with him and and what do you feel like if it if it turns out that way that you two bring to the table for a first team defense? >> Yeah, I mean uh we definitely been growing. Uh we like playing playing more with beside each other. Um just talking and feeling off of each other. Just seeing how each other play and like playing styles and being able I don't know kind of like read each other's mind on how he likes to play and how I like to play and just uh being able to execute whatever the play call is. Um uh Uh I mean he's physical he's fast he can cover things that Lou wants out of linebackers and we just got to keep stacking days stacking weeks. >> Have you ever had a safety wear the green dot in your career and I guess what's it been like just transitioning to that? >> Yeah actually Cincinnati our first year cuz I mean uh we had a young room just like kind of like similar to here and Vonn Bell he kind of wore the green dot. Got to be on the field the whole time throughout the the three down so yeah. >> So that you know the defense so well have you seen some progression from Lou and even added some tweaks to it that you said oh I like that one. >> Yeah yeah I mean yeah I mean I can tell you what the play call is >> No I mean we definitely definitely added a added a few in there but similar thing but like you said added a little little tweaks in there some some stuff we seen that he might like in the first couple weeks that that's going to help us play faster help us execute some things that we like against the opponent so it most definitely done tweaked some things added some things since I last been with him. >> All right thank you Keanu. Thank you Keanu. >> For you having this stretch of consistency consecutive weeks stacking the days is just how grateful are you to get through training camp be at this point going to preseason prepping for the regular season and really just be healthy. >> It's a blessing you know going into my third year you know having some some mishaps in my second year also getting injured my first year just a blessing to be healthy coming into this year and be able to play with my teammates again. >> In the time that you were away and you were rehabbing how did you try to stay engaged so when you were healthy and ready to go you could take advantage of the opportunities as you seemingly have in this camp. >> Uh consistently talking with my coaches you know asking questions in meetings consistently still going to meetings watching practice when I'm able to and things like that just always kept me in the loop and always just kept my mental good as well you know just being around my teammates and my coaches is just kept me involved and it just made me feel like I was still welcome here. >> I know we've seen you and Akeem take a lot of the first team reps at linebacker over the last week or two. What what do you feel like the chemistry is between you two guys and what you could bring to a first team unit if you guys do play a lot together? >> Akeem came to vet in the room, you know, Akeem definitely helps everybody out. He helps us out on the field, he helps us out off the field, you know, whenever we have questions, he answers them. And so, you know, when I always have questions, you know, I'll ask him and he does his best every time to help me out and it's always you just you just clicking on all cylinders after that. So, you know, it's it's a blessing to really have him beside me. Especially just in our room in general cuz, you know, we're a real young room. So, just being able to have that vet experience with Akeem is just helps us out a lot. >> Jaylen, you you always feel really comfortable in coverage, obviously, but it felt like this training camp you took a real step forward in terms of working downhill and making plays in the run game. Even though you've been out, do you just feel more comfortable being a linebacker now? >> I definitely feel more comfortable being a linebacker cuz it all just comes with reps, you know, whether it's mental reps or whether it's physically getting them. You know, it starts with just being able to see it see the picture and then once you're able to get into the system and actually do the plays, you know, and be do the assignments that you're given, it helps out a lot and it's made it's made me real comfortable as well. Like I said, you know, with missing last year not even really being able to get those reps during the season. Coming through OTAs and this training camp and off season, getting these reps now has definitely made me more comfortable in the position. >> I know you mentioned the reps. Entering year three besides health, what specifically are you looking at to say, "Okay, this is where I need to grow or have grown as a linebacker?" >> You know, talking with my coaches, you know, they're giving us stuff throughout OTAs and training camp and different things like that and we write them down. Coach Betts always tells us write down two things you need to work on today, you know, and we put we put those two things in our notes and we all try to execute them when we come back out here and I feel like I'm I'm making those steps and progressing forward with doing those things. You know, there's always still something to work on that I can get better at and I just continue to try to prove that and I drive with that as well.

title: Jobs on the line: Texans vs. Panthers preseason finale, Braden Smith, Ali Gaye injury details
text: You guys made the trip. >> Oh, we did. >> Hey guys, Aaron Wilson here in Charlotte, North Carolina where the Texans will take on the Carolina Panthers in the third and final preseason game Friday night at Bank of America Stadium. The Texans of course had their joint practice session with the Panthers which they dominated and we talked about that in another video. We'll have some more observations, but let's start with the news and it's a mix of relatively good news and some very bad news. So, first the relatively good news. Offensive tackle Brain Smith, the veteran they signed to a two-year $25 million contract this off seasonason. He has suffered a partially torn plantar fascia in his foot. I first reported this in the morning and want to discuss and break down the, you know, the impact of this. Now, so it is a good news situation in the sense that it's not a long-term injury. He could return in a few weeks. So, there's optimism from the team about his outlook medically. Of course, what this means in the interim is the right tackle competition is over and that means Trent Brown is your starting right tackle and he was already obviously listed on the depth chart that way and started against Las Vegas Raiders. As Deo Ryan has said many times, it's tough to go around him. Takes a long time and it's very tough if not impossible to go through him. He is massive. He is 6'8. He is 400 lb. He's a former Pro Bowl selection. He was the starting left tackle for the New England Patriots when they won the Super Bowl in 2018. So, he's a lot of things and he's also a Bassrop native, a rancher, cattleman, all those good things. So, with Big Trent there, this increases the importance of Blake Fiser and De Mo Ryan. You'll hear from De Mo with a lot of praise for Blake Fischer called him their most improved offensive lineman. That's important. He's a former second round draft pick from Notre Dame, former consensus all-American that has started 15 career games. He has not lived up the expectations in the sense that he hasn't won a permanent starting job and they've keep bringing people and putting them ahead of him on the lineup and on the depth chart. So, what I see from Blake, I see a real seriousness. My understanding is that he has been here and been here but been with the Texans in terms of offseason training as early as possible that he could be in the offseason program and then not missing days that he was just very dedicated. This was a new version of Blake Fischer, a more serious, a more mature Blake Fischer in his third year. So those are all good things. And not to bury the lead, but obviously, you know, talk about the player that was uh nearly in the starting lineup first. And this is the bad news, very bad news. And it's defensive end Ali Gay. And Ali has suffered a major injury so severe that he'll get multiple second opinions per sources. And I reported this earlier today. And so this is something that is going to be a surgical situation and he will need to miss the entire season. So injured reserve, it's a very bad development for Ali who we don't know if he would have made the 15 man roster but he was certainly you know with all the injuries they've had he was going to get a you know shot he was in the contention very big player 66 265 lbs and so this further thins the defensive end core of course we know they have Denil Hunter Anderson Jr. of those guys are blue chip at the top of the game, the top pass rushing tandem combining for 27 sacks last year and just not just the sacks, it's the pressure, it's the hurries, it's intimidation, it's the moves, it's all the great things with those guys. However, Javian Clowney is sidelined currently with an ankle injury. It's not considered long term. So, they'll get him back. And then you look at Dominique Robinson. It's been weeks since he's practiced. He's got a calf injury. he's getting better and they expect both guys to be back for the season. So that would fill out the first four defensive end spots in my opinion. So they had to sign Derrick Parish because they lost Dylan Horton to a torn Achilles. So all these are tough injury fallout situations where the Texans have taken on some water there at the defensive end position. I'll anticipate the question because you want to know who's not playing due to injury or other reasons against the Carolina Panthers. So, let's start with the fact the starters are not slated to play. So, no starters will play. Of course, I consider the specialist starters. So, that means Kaimi Farber, the kicker, the punter, Kai Krueger. We were worried about Kai Krueger and not anymore. Kai Krueger's been very good. And long snapper Austin Brinkman. So, you have to have the specialist. They don't have any backup specialists. They tried that with Chris Freeman, the kicker, to give Kaim a break. Didn't wind up working out. Ka kicked very well against the Panthers in practice, by the way. So, without any further ado, let's run down who's not healthy enough to play against the Panthers. So, we start with, of course, Javian Clowney with an ankle, Dominique Robinson with a calf, then the running backs. Jabar Jordan, that strained hip flexor took a lot longer. He is still sidelineed. They still hope to get him back in time for the season. They got British Brooks back from a broken hand and that took about three weeks. Rookie running back Noah Winningington is sidelineed with an ankle injury. He won't play this game. Linebacker Wade Wood had successful surgery Monday for his broken thumb and he's going to miss this entire week and then try to practice next week with a cast on. Of course, linebacker Jake Hansen got hurt early in camp, has been running for weeks now on the side nearing his return. Tight end Brevin Jordan has a knee injury and this is pre-existing from the torn patellar tendon from the torn ACL over the past two years. So, uh it's not going a good direction for Brevin. Unfortunate wide receiver Tank Dell and Tank has been working independently with the team, you know, on the side and also with his own private training staff. And the idea is that they could get him ready for later in the season. And we get a lot of questions about this.
