title: Post-Game Press Conference with Sean McVay & Ty Simpson Following Preseason Win Over the Chargers
text: A lot of our coaches to get experiences that I've kind of shared that I got a chance to get when I was in some different roles and I thought really just the way that our guys improved, but really proud of them. And and you know, and now here we go. We're looking forward to being able to start our preparation on the 49ers. We know what a great challenge it's going to be. We've got some tough decisions over the next couple days to make and the cool thing is the guys that have been playing have made it tough for us and that's that's a positive thing for us for the depth of our roster. I'm sure you guys are wondering, you know, be good to be able to bring too too Atwell back. Obviously wish Jaquess Hunter nothing but the best moving forward. Felt like it was a chance to be able to, you know, add depth to the receiver room. Kind of know, you know, there's a good feel for those top three backs that we that we saw and I thought both Jordan and and Dean did a really nice job of, you know, solidifying that they're they're real factors that, you know, you got to be able to take into consideration what does that look like? So, thought the quarterbacks, I thought Ty played really well tonight. Going into it, you know, that I wouldn't look too far into what that was. It was just continuing to get him experience. We've got three quarterbacks on our roster. Obviously, we've got the reigning MVP of the league and then we got two guys that we feel really good about. And if you say, "Hey, what does that really mean?" That's what it means. We feel too really good about those two guys. Not pigeonholing myself into any sort of decision other than I feel really good about Stetson Bennett, feel really good about Ty Simpson and I hope Matthew Caldwell's okay. It was good to be able to get him in there and see him do some really good things. Hopefully his knee's going to be all right and with that I'll take your guys' questions. >> Coach, on that pass uh letting your test on pads uh by Ty >> Yeah. >> Was that as a glimpse into what his potential is? >> I think so. You know, I think some of the fun things then is to see are, you know, the off schedule. You know, there was a it was a pressure look. They lost contain on the pressure. He escaped it, kept his eyes down the field and Brandon Presley did a great job of being able to work off schedule with him. But I think in the games you've really seen a lot of really good things from him in each of these last three games. Didn't have as much opportunities last week, tonight, and obviously in week one and um been really pleased with Ty. He did a great job. I thought he had good command. He's got a great game day demeanor. It was good to see him do his thing tonight. >> Was the trade for Tutu made as kind of a preemptive thing in case Puka is suspended? >> No. No, it had nothing to do with that. It was exclusively guy that we were familiar with that you could really get at what we felt like was um you know, good for us and good for Jarquez. And and that was uh you know, he I think he'll do a good job for the Dolphins and it's never easy when you have guys that are such great people, but uh we're familiar with Tutu. He adds depth, you know, it gives us an opportunity to be able to have that speed element and he can do some different things. That it had nothing to do with anything other than just adding depth to the receiver room. >> Guys, last last year the the Chargers had a they touted a top-five defense. Today, uh Ty Simpson looked extremely comfortable under center. Can you just talk to me about his game, his performance that you saw from him? >> Yeah, I thought he was in good command. I thought he made good decisions. I thought he, you know, went where the ball was supposed to go. Uh you know, just like what Dennis was asking. And then the cool thing is is some of the second reaction plays, you know, when it doesn't necessarily work out in rhythm and you were able to escape and buy time. Thought even in the bootleg game, he did a great job of attacking the edge, finding to just be able to keep the ball in play, and managing the run game. They did you know, they were bringing everything that they've got, you know, and so um you know, it'll be they're they're really good defense. They're going to be a really good football team, but I thought Ty did a great job tonight. >> Guys, as you as you as the preseason is now over, um do you like where the team is at this point? >> I do. You know, and and there's always, you know, we're it's never-ending constant evolution and improvement, constant growth. That's really what we want to be about. That's why we always talk about just stacking days, but what I thought the preseason represented was a great opportunity to be able to celebrate a lot of guys that don't even get a ton of practice reps. And uh I thought they, you know, really did a great job of of showing well for themselves, whether that's for us or for other teams. Um I love the vibe that I felt from our coaching staff in terms of working with our players and even the the guys that weren't playing the way that they were able to celebrate their teammates each other the last few weeks and um, you know, forever it's going to be tough because, you know, I look at it as we got 70 guys that'll be on our football team. It's 53 but then you got your, you know, 16 practice squad and then you have the one international. So, you got 70 guys and we got 20 tough decisions to make and um, and then really even some of the 53 decisions are going to be really difficult but that's a positive based on what this locker room is about. So, I was uh, I was pleased knowing that there's a lot of growth ahead and it's crazy to think that 2 weeks from tonight we'll be uh, playing in Australia. So, here we go. >> Is this come board, guys? Shawn, does that seems Is that unique in terms of because it's in Australia and it is 2 weeks away or is it wake up tomorrow morning and you're a Niner? >> Yeah, I mean, I've been on the night You know, it's one of those deals. The answer is yes, it is unique, you know, I mean, we when we in the 22 season when we opened on that Thursday night but it it's it's a little bit different rhythm and routine where even some of the mandated days off that typically, you know, uh, end up being on like Friday, Saturday, Sunday or Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday for us, you know, moving forward. So, it's a little bit different but hey, we we we'll have a unique schedule in general just based on it seems like we play on every day of the week this year. So, that won't be an excuse. We'll be ready to go and uh, I'm excited to get going with this team. >> You said Aaron has uh, earned the right to make the decision on his timeline but do you expect him to make a decision and it to be a quick process to get on the roster and deal with the contract or do you think it might take time for when he tells you that he wants to return for him to be back on the roster? >> I think all of those things are up in the air, you know, and and I I wish I had a little bit better, you know, ability to give you some clarity but it's really one of those deals that, you know, what what what we're doing, we're focusing on this football team. Aaron knows that, hey, if he wants to be able to do that, that's something that we absolutely want to entertain and be able to figure out. Um, and that's really kind of all there is to it right now. >> With adding Tutu, uh, um, you know, you feel like you have a lot of receiver options that are doing pretty well as it is. So, um, when you talk about making tough decisions, are you confident that you'll be able to keep as many as you feel like have earned that right? Every receiver? >> Yeah. Oh, yeah. Yeah, part of it there there's some semantics that you guys will see when when our 53 comes out that, you know, we have a couple things that we can do that creatively give us an opportunity to be able to onboard Tutu without affecting any of the guys that would have been originally slotted for, you know, what we projected as our 53. >> Sean, did you talk to Tutu today? >> Oh, yeah. Absolutely. >> So, what was his reaction, if you could, about coming back? >> I think he was excited. You know, I think he enjoyed his time at Miami and, um, you know, I said, "You don't have a choice. You're coming here, you know?" So, it didn't really matter whether he wanted to or not. But, it's, uh, I love Tutu. There's a lot of love for Tutu out well in this locker room and a lot of familiarity. And so, I know Miami's home for him, but this is his second home. So, we're excited to be able to welcome him back. Okay? Thanks, guys. >> Hey, you guys got time for Stetson to come in? >> Um, yeah. Uh, with, you know, more reps, more time. It's understanding everything. Um, you know, Matthew and Stetson helping me out every chance I can get. Um, you know, I feel really good, uh, with where I'm at. Um, but, you know, I still got a, you know, a lot I need to work on. >> Talking about last year, the Chargers touted you to the top five in the league. Can you just talk to me about the the speed of the game? How does How does things feel for you in the pocket? >> Yeah, um, you know, it definitely is faster, for sure. I knew they're, um, their starters were going to play at least the first series. Um, my dad actually told me that. Um, but I was, uh, I was excited cuz it was my first time to where, you know, I was going against, you know, real guys in a real game. Um and and you know, it felt like I expected to feel, you know, fast, have to make quick decisions, um you know, knowing, you know, where my outlets are. Um and it just felt good to be out there. >> Ty, can you walk us through the the 11-yard touchdown pass in the corner of the end zone and just kind of how that came together? >> Uh yeah. Um you know, me and Rags kind of went through some stuff um yesterday, 2 days ago of, you know, just um some blitzes and third downs and stuff. Um so, I kind of had an idea that in the red zone, you know, they were going to go man. Um there was some miscommunication on the line with a funky front. Um you know, and I tried not to take it a negative play and BP did a good job of, you know, playing football, uh getting open. Um and I just tried to get the, you know, good player the ball. >> Do you feel as comfortable moving to the left as to the right? You've done some of both of that preseason. How does that feel for you? >> you know, I I I think that as a quarterback, right? Like you got to be, you know, ambidextrous as much as you can. You know, not as um everybody, you know, feels comfortable throwing to the right, but if you can throw it to the left, too, like it makes, you know, it hard on defenses. And and I think Sean and Nathan, you know, Rags do a, you know, great job of emphasizing that in practice of, you know, making sure that, you know, we get our shoulders, you know, turned and making sure that, you know, we make every throw to the left just as much as we do the right. Um and so, you know, I try to make that match up as best as I can. >> Ty, throughout camp and and throughout the preseason, um there has been tremendous comfort uh chemistry with CJ Daniels. Can you just talk to me about how that has developed and and how do you got how do you how has it played out for you? >> Um yeah, you know, I knew CJ um you know, coming in the draft process just because of um seeing what he did at Miami. Um you know, I'm good friends with Carson Beck, so I I knew that uh you know, he had a good chemistry with him. Um and then his teammate James Rockermaier, who's a former teammate of mine. Um and then, you know, meeting him when we drafted him, um, I could tell his maturity. You can tell like his, um, love for the game and you know, how he loved to work. We would, you know, on OTAs he would want to meet on weekends and, um, go over, you know, walkthroughs and understand the rules of a quarterback and just, you know, be be a sponge and soak everything up. Um, so coming in here together, me, him, Max Clark, um, Keegan, um, all those guys on offense is trying to stay together as a rookie class and just try to build, you know, the chemistry and understand that like, you know, hey, we want to make an impact as best as we could. Um, and you know, he's been a blanket for me. He knows what to do on every play. He's a great football player and just, you know, he's a savvy, mature, you know, person and I and I really really enjoy being a teammate of his. >> And on this team, regardless of, you know, you knew where you were going to be behind Matthew regardless of you whether you're second or third on that list. What did you feel like you've learned through this preseason experience getting that opportunity to to play with the offense? >> Yeah. Um, you know, one just a just a turn of ball. Just, you know, understanding the offense in general of what, you know, Sean and Nate emphasized of, you know, what we want to, you know, be our identity, um, and you know, our separators as an offense. Um, learning that through the, you know, couple couple months has really, you know, I felt like taking my game to another level of just understanding overall like, hey, you know, this is how the NFL game is cuz it's a different than in college game. Um, you know, I feel like I've, um, you know, even though I didn't play much in college, being around my dad and being around, you know, other good college football players like Bryce and Jaylen, I know, um, you know, the game pretty well and then coming here and, you know, learning from Sean who's been in it and one of the best, you know, learning from Matthew who is, you know, the best and then, you know, learning from Stetson and just, you know, everything that I've learned these, you know, last couple months has has been grateful. Um, and you know, I'm really looking forward to the, you know, the season and you know, years to come. >> How do you feel like you've grasped grasped the playbook and what have been the challenges of learning this playbook? >> Um, yeah, you know, I still don't know it, you know, like I, um, want to, you know, I want to know the ins and outs of everything, the whys. You know, but I do feel like I have a better understanding each and every day I go in the work. Just understanding like, you know, hey, these are our rules. You know, hey, this is we want this to look like this. And then just, you know, technique. You know, hey, like, you know, on this play like it's going to be hard for you to look at this route, right? But like, you know, try to make it match it up so we can manipulate the defense and you know, that's why it's so, you know, great to be in a room with two great guys and rags who, you know, help a young guy like myself, but also can do it at a high level, you know, with Stetson and Matthew. >> Hey, Ty, talk about adversity. Not getting a lot of reps, but still asked to be productive. >> Yeah, you know, I think adversity, you know, starts in my college career, right? You know, not playing many games, didn't get to start in my fourth year, but, you know, always trying to be better and be the best guy I could be and, you know, when that opportunity comes to, you know, make the most of it. You know, there was a time in college to where I did get an opportunity. I didn't capitalize and then I told myself I was never going to do that again. So I knew coming in, you know, to this organization that it was Matthew's team and, you know, I was going to be behind him, but I told myself, right? Like, regardless of the circumstance, like I'm always going to be mentally ready and always going to be prepared like I'm going to play because it's only it's only going to help you. You know, there's no, you know, pity parties for you sitting around saying I wish I could be back in college or I wish I could be you know, on another team or another organization. That does, you know, no good. You got to be where your feet are. You know, Sean says it all the time, be present. Well, you know, I'm present as a, you know, backup quarterback on the Los Angeles Rams to, you know, two really good, you know, quarterbacks and really good human beings. And so, you know, taking as much, you know, reps as I can and asking questions. And I say this all the time, you know, Matthew and Stetson probably think I'm the annoying little kid, little brother because I ask him so many questions, but it really helps me a lot. So, you know, the adversity comes, but you know, it's you know, pipes water it makes diamonds or bust. So, you know, just got to keep going. >> Has coach communicated to you Has coach communicated to you whether you'll be the backup quarterback in Australia? >> Yeah, you know, I I don't really ask him that. You know, I kind of just do what I'm told and go in when I go in. You know, I think it really doesn't really matter if I'm being honest like what I am um cuz this is Matthew Stafford and you know, I'm behind him 100% and I know Stetson is and there's nobody you know, his biggest fans besides us two. And you know, he has our support 100% and you know, that's all that really matters. >> Ty, now that the regular season is here, the team is getting ready to prepare for the ultimate Swiss Army knife in Christian McCaffrey. You have Dean Conners who today shown tremendous ability to run inside the tackles, outside, catch the ball out of the backfield. Can you just talk to me about the level of versatility that he brings to the team and as a quarterback, how does that type of versatility help you? >> Yeah, it's a little McCaffrey is what he is. Um but it helps us a lot, right? Like you saw him, you know, do it all preseason. He can, you know, do it all from, you know, run downhill to run out wide to run routes. You know, he he talks about Christian all the time. I know he works out with him. But it helps us, right? Because we can do so many things. You look at all our backs, right? Like they're all the same type of scat back to where, you know, you can, you know, put them out wide to run a, you know, a route or they can run downhill, they got great vision. So, you know, shout out to all those guys and and Dean's done a great job. So, having him is, you know, really really resourceful and I'm looking forward to, you know, seeing seeing what he does. >> Awesome. Thank you. >> Yeah, thanks Ty. Thanks, Ty. >> Mhm.

Um, and so, you know, a lot to correct and, um, you know, we'll get back better. >> Can you elaborate on why you good for me to see? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, some adversity for the first time in the NFL. title: What Roster Moves Will Matter Most for the Seahawks?
text: I don't know. I think that what might help Jaylen Milroe is there doesn't seem to be a a great debate as to who's going to be say the 51st player on this roster right now. I there it it does seem fairly predictable and these things always a little bit unpredictable but I don't think there's a huge mystery as to who's actually going to make this team. And if there were 56 players that they wanted to keep and they needed to keep a a bit of extra depth say at a receiver or safety or whatever because of the injuries or any other position for that matter, I think Milroe could be in trouble because I just think we've here's what we've seen now. We've seen a fairly unimpressive if you're being honest final season at Alabama where he he did not play very well in a lot of the games. He had 16 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, not great numbers in your final year of college football. A lot of those touchdowns come against opponents like Western Kentucky and Mercer. So he didn't have a touchdown against LSU. He didn't have a touchdown against Missouri. He didn't have a touchdown against Oklahoma. Oklahoma. And he and he came into the draft in in 2025 with no real momentum behind his stock. Now, didn't have a good senior bowl. Didn't have a great combine but the physical tools, the fact that he's not going to bad arm and he is quick and that Georgia game where he exploded with his arm and his legs obviously stuck in the memory. He's great character guy. Seahawks took a chance with him. But when he was given a big opportunity against Green Bay last preseason, he didn't take it. It's his first season in the league, okay. You can kind of give him a mulligan for that one. We've watched two preseason games now. He's throwing a shade over 50% of completing a shade over 50% completions. He is holding onto the football. He's not showing any anticipation in the pocket. He's not throwing with um that that great level of accuracy. Look at the the interception he had the other day. I I I just don't think it In my opinion and I and I don't think need a lot of evidence to really come to this conclusion. I don't think he's an NFL quarterback. And I think the only way that I've written about this today, I think the only way that he's going to salvage his career right now and stick in the league is to show I can score points, I can make plays, and I'm going to use my superpower to do it, which is his speed and his ability as a runner. He seems really hesitant towards that, as we saw with Mike McDonald basically pleading with him to use his legs more. He doesn't seem to want to do that. He had a 16-yard run against the Titans and didn't have another running attempt in the whole game after that. He led an offense that didn't score a single point in that game. He threw an awful interception. He took an awful sack on fourth down. Uh there was another interception which maybe it's not totally his fault. Don't think it was most accurate pass, either. I think he he's got to go now and run and make plays and show because I don't think Jaylen Milroe's ever going to be a 17-game starter in the NFL year after year franchise quarterback. There's not many of those in the league. There's not 32 franchise quarterbacks in the NFL. The chances of him becoming one was always remote. He has got to show that he has some value in this league, though. So that if he's going to be a backup quarterback, which might be his his ceiling, frankly, that if you need him to play one game, two games, four games, whatever it is, he can make some plays for you. He can he can lead a drive, but do it in his way, using his style, which is to be a runner, and to play off that, not to sit in the pocket patting the football, waiting for somebody to come wide open, and then when he sees the wide open throw, try and deliver the pass, and it's too late. And often he's sort of sat there and he and then he sets off and he takes a sack. That's not going to be good enough. So, I think the evidence from last preseason in terms of the games, cuz that's all I can watch, and the two games you've seen this year, it's it's to me, he just looks like a bad quarterback. So, I'm play I would play He's not going to listen to this, but I would play with him. Go to your superpower. That is your ability to make plays on the move. Be creative. Scramble around. Get outside, set off and run. Show the league, show the Seahawks, show the fans that you can make things happen. Lead drives, score points. Cuz you're not doing it with your arm. >> Hey y'all, this year I moved to Nashville, Tennessee, where there is always a concert, game, or live event to go see. And it's hard to keep track of it all. That's why I use SeatGeek, where you can find over 70,000 events listed. And right now, I got my eye on the Music City Kickoff. Country music and college football? I think that should work. And SeatGeek has your back. Every ticket is rated on a scale of 1 to 10, so you know exactly what you're getting. Plus, every ticket is backed by a buyer's guarantee. This app is so helpful to sift through all the different games, festivals, and concerts. So, write this down, because there's a code just for you. Use collective10 for 10% off your next tickets at SeatGeek. Just download the app, use collective10, and if you're going to go, go with SeatGeek. >> Well, you mentioned it, too. Well, you mentioned it. No, no, I I want to I want to toss it to you on this, but Rob Brian, while you were out for a second, did mention just how we did get to see that clip of Mike McDonald encouraging Jalen Milroe to use his legs and in his superpower and run and and be dangerous. And sometimes, even as an athlete, when you're able to early in a game use what your strength is, like hit your best shot, hit somebody, make physical contact early on, it can kind of loosen you up and get and give you some confidence as well. But, yeah, I would love your thoughts on Jalen Milroe, but also maybe just the confidence that you have in the backup quarterback and Drew Lock headed into the regular season. >> Yeah, I'll I'll try to remember to get back to Drew Lock, who I think I mean maybe I'll just start there, cuz I think it's pretty straightforward. Drew Lock is a perfectly good backup quarterback in this league. He could be a starter for some of the teams in this league. Uh, I don't think he's a top half of the league starter or a guy that you'd feel really confident in, but I think he's a really good guy that you could win a few games with if you needed to. As far as Jaylen Milroe, part of the reason I love this topic is I find myself in a really fun position. And I I I I'm a weird in the fact that I find this a fun position. This is a guy who I was admittedly against as a quarterback prospect in college. I just I never saw it. I didn't like his style of play. I didn't think his decision-making was good. I didn't think his accuracy was good. It was just like I didn't get the hype. Just didn't get it. I was really low on him, you know, coming through the draft process. And now I'm in this position where I'm maybe the only one outside of the building and maybe outside of Jaylen's family that hasn't given up on him. Like I I don't see it near like I see in comments like he will definitely never be drop-back quarterback in the NFL, a pocket passer in the NFL. Based on what? One season? One season in the NFL? Uh, his first season as a under center Kubiak, Shanahan-style offense, play-action, pro-style offense after running spread and at sometimes like wildcat in college? What are you talking about? Like I I I I think that that's crazy to be that definitive at this point. I fully understand why you'd say I have seen nothing to make me think he could be that person. Like there's no sign that he I I I actually don't agree with that either, but I can understand that perspective. But to be definitive about the fact that he will never be after one season, after all that we've learned about quarterback development in this league is wild to me. So, the the other part of this that I I I also really love is to to take that position, I think, isn't a hard position to take. I would say the chance that any quarterback that comes into the NFL that they're going to develop into a franchise quarterback is less than 50%. And if you're taking in the third round and you're talking about the developmental requirements or like the the slope that you're asking him to climb is way less than 50%. Even I, someone who has not given up on him as a prospect, think that there's less than a 30% chance that he develops into a quarterback of interest. I'm just saying there's not like a 0% chance. I don't even think there's only a 10% chance. I think there's there's a there's a small chance that he still could develop into that. And so the other part that I really find fun about this is he's a third-round pick and he's a third-string quarterback. >> [laughter] >> It just doesn't Like it matters to him, it matters to us to have these debates. Like I see Rob like, you know, not thrilled with with my position on this and I love it cuz Rob and I see a lot of things the same way. >> slouch. >> I know, he's like, "I don't like anything this guy's saying." But but like I love that we can have these like somewhat meaningless debates and I say that lightly because it is meaningful a lot to, you know, Jaylen and and folks involved, but it's just it's it's not it's not going to determine whether the Seahawks are an interesting team this year. Probably not going to determine whether the Seahawks are an interesting team next year. It is the only thing that's going to determine is do the Seahawks have value in Jaylen Milroe. And one of the things I think I'm hearing from Rob is he's already like, "It's not going to be as a quarterback and it's not going to be as a starting quarterback." So, find or it's it's not going to be as a typical starting quarterback, find something else that you can show your value. I'm fine with that, but I also I have seen I thought there were really good throws from him in this game. I think there were just some really bad decisions. And if I listed for you all the quarterbacks that have come into this league that made bad decisions in their first two years in the league that then went on to make better decisions and become better players, it's a pretty sizable list.

title: 49ers 18, Raiders 12: Preseason Grades
text: The San Francisco 49ers just beat the Las Vegas Raiders 18-12 in the preseason finale. Here are the grades for their performance. Quarterbacks C minus. M. Jones played only two series and never got into the flow of the game because his receivers weren't open. More on them in a minute. Jones finished the night completing just one of five pass attempts for seven yards and his passer rating was 39.6. It would have been nice to see him play a third series just so he could get an opportunity to do something positive. Instead, [snorts] the Niners quickly yanked him for Adrien Martinez, who made some decent plays, but won't make the 53man roster, nor should he. It's too bad the Niners gave so much playing time during the season to this practice squad quarterback who has no future on their team or in the NFL. It's also too bad that Curtis Ror broke three ribs running a quarterback draw near the goal line in the preseason opener. He looked good like someone who could be Brock Pery's main backup next year when Jones leaves. Running backs a minus. Jordan James made his preseason debut and gained 55 yards from scrimmage on nine touches. He's quick, he can catch, and he runs with no hesitation. He's a good all-around backup running back. I can't believe the Niners played Brian Robinson Jr. over him last season. That was silly. The best running back tonight was Kaylin Black, who wasn't targeted and missed a key block on one of M. Jones deep, incomplete passes, so he still has much to prove in the passing game, but in the running game, he was a monster as usual. In this game, he gained 28 yards on four carries. That's seven yards per attempt. He clearly is the most explosive ball carrier on the team. No disrespect to Christian McCaffrey. He used to be the team's most explosive back, but now he's older. Wide receivers D. They were terrible. Jordan Watkins got a chance to show something against the Raiders starters who aren't particularly good, and he responded by catching one of three targets for 5 yards. Twice he was targeted deep, and both times he did nothing to shake the defender and get himself open. On the first deep target, Watkins didn't even bother to turn his head and find the ball. He was just out for a leisurely jog as if he already had made the team. in this third preseason game was a mere formality. Watkins isn't nearly good enough to play that way. That's why he had to stay on the field all night. Take a hint, Jordan. And he was by far the Niners's best receiver in the game. None of these players run good routes. The Niners desperately need Dejon Stribbling to stay healthy and produce 1,000 yards this season. Tight ends B. Hayden Ruchcci had two first downs and a touchdown catch that got called back due to a low block by Jordan James. If the Niners keep four tight ends, which they should and probably will, then the fourth tight end should be Roocci, not Braden Willis, who left this game early with a concussion. Offensive lineman, a the 49ers rushed the ball well all night and took just one sack. Granted, they were facing the Raiders, who were terrible. Still, the offensive line performed well without most of their starters. Defensive linemen, C. Alfred Collins and CJ West were abysmal. Both guys repeatedly got blown off the ball in the running game. Whenever they came out, the run defense improved. Both Collins and Wes seemed out of shape. Neither one currently can hold his ground or disengage from blocks. They're not in danger of getting released, but Collins in particular is supposed to be a starter and they can't afford to play him right now. Their best healthy defensive lineman who played tonight is Keon White, who sacked Fernando Mendoza after bulldozing the center. In addition, backup defensive end, Ogbo Okarano, sacked Mendoza, too. Okarano absolutely has done enough to make this team. Linebackers C. The best linebacker was Tatum Bthun, who finished with nine tackles and an interception. Rookie Jaden Duggar played into the third quarter and recorded a team high 10 tackles and two quarterback hits. He also missed two tackles he should have made. So, he's still a work in progress and he has a ton of potential, but he's a bit of a liability as an inside linebacker off the line of scrimmage, defending runs between the tackles. He seems much more comfortable as an outside linebacker on the line of scrimmage, setting edges, dropping into coverage and blitzing. Defensive backs B+. Ashton Davis started at safety and missed a tackle. He shouldn't make the team. Siron Neil played great at quarterback in the first half despite getting flagged for a bogus pass interference call. Jack Jones also broke up a pass. He does that a lot. He'll start week one if Bernardo Green isn't back from his hamstring injury. And rookie Ephesians Pryog left the game with a shoulder injury and quickly was ruled out. That doesn't sound good. Special teams a Eddie Panero made all six of his field goal attempts including a 59yder. He unironically is one of the five best players on the roster. The Niners wouldn't have made the playoffs without him last season.

title: Cam Ward on Carnell Tate's Big Day & Trusting Brian Daboll | Press Conference
text: Poor start for sure. Um, but I think as, you know, we got we got going, you know, the energy started to pick up. Um, we started being more efficient in the pass game, being more efficient in the run game. Uh, but overall it was a pretty good day. >> And then Alshon took a a pretty hard hit. Did you get a chance to talk to him? What was your >> Uh, yeah, he's good. Um, I got to put him in a better situation. Uh, so that that's really more of on me than on him. Um, but you know, he he's tough. Um, he's going to have to take a hit like that, you know, this season. Um, I'm doing my best to try to prevent that as much as I can throwing the ball. Um, but I mean, he's he he got up, he's good, and you know, I'm going to make sure I don't put to him in that position again. >> You saw you target Tate a lot today. Was part of that intentional, or was that just where your reads were going, or was it behind so many targets to to 14? >> Um, he was open. Um, honestly. Uh, you know, giving me a step on the defender, um, then me and him also continue to, you know, grow together, me putting the ball in a in a radius where he can make a play on it. Um, and then him also, you know, making a play on when I'm not as accurate. Um, so it is vice versa. Um, but you know, he he had a he had a pretty good day. He showed why, you know, uh, he was that pick. Um, but me and him it's more of us, you know, continuing to, you know, be consistent. Um, whether I'm going to him a lot, or I'm going to him, you know, one time. Um, me and him have to continue to be in the same mindset that, you know, we're the go-getters, and we got to make the plays. >> How encouraging was it? There was one you scrambled to your right, he broke his route off, worked his way back to you. How encouraging was it to see you guys at very much on the same page on the scramble? >> Oh, that's great. Um, that's something that we, you know, we watch tape on each and every day scramble drill. Uh, they know it's going to be a big part of our offense. Um, so we're going to be able to hit explosives. Um, we're going to be able to There's going to be throwaways in scramble drill, but as long as we have our angles right, and knowing when to, you know, go upfield, when to come back down towards me. Um, I think it's going to be able to help us in the long run. Um, he had a great day in scramble drill. >> You guys have both talked working on that connection. Is that a progress on Do you guys take a big step forward today doing what you did together against the opponent? >> Uh I just think it was just routine plays for me and him. Um It's really more of me and him, you know, trusting each other each and every down. Um and whether it's not a great route or whether it's not a great ball by myself, um me and him are continuously getting on that on that connection to where is I can always trust him, he can always trust me. Uh there's going to be times that I told him today, you know, you going to have to bail me out. There's going to be times where, you know, I got to put the ball in the perfect spot, he got to make a play. Um but it's really just me and him continue to, you know, learn each other, continue to, you know, be in a real game atmosphere, whether it's, you know, in the preseason game or whether it's in practice versus a different team. Um then us just continue to be more consistent in myself putting the ball in his frame. >> You and the first team offense can't have one more opportunity in the preseason. How how important is it for you guys to put together some some consistency to go out on before the real game begins? >> Uh it's important. Um just need to show consistent plays in, you know, the first and second down. Um we haven't really been in any major third and long so far. Um so I think the more we can play efficient on first and second down, we're going to be able to take care of everything and then we'll be able to score, you know, some more points. >> Cam, how much do you and Caleb in that pretty exclusive club of the number one overall picks quarterbacks? Do you know him at all? Have you met and talked to him? >> Yeah, I met him before. Uh had some conversations with him. >> What did What do you guys talk about? >> Um stuff outside football, honestly. Um he's whether he's whether he's good mentally, uh whether his fam his fam is good, healthy. Uh my dad and his dad, you know, they talk a whole bunch. Um and so, you know, it's good because, you know, he's a he's a good quarterback. Uh he took his team to the playoffs. And so, you know, we we both go through different situations, different types of adversity, um whether they can be early or late. Um but I mean, it's good to have, you know, uh another, you know, good quarterback out here on the field, that way our defense can get some good work in. >> Cam, why do you guys practice better against first team defenses than you guys have played against second team defenses in the games. >> Uh I just think more of the the practice we're doing more game stuff that we can do in a real football game. Uh it's a lot of stuff that, you know, we don't want to put on tape to show in the preseason game that doesn't matter. Um it's more of, you know, getting better at the stuff that we know we're going to do come week one and week two and week three. Um and then, you know, it's a it's a difference when, you know, you you know you know, the the the certain types of plays that we're putting in each and every week compared to, you know, every play is in. So, uh it's a little bit of everything, but at the end of the day there's no excuses, you know, no matter we play the ones, twos, or threes and they're in the field, ain't no backups. It's the reason why, you know, they're on the roster right now. It's the reason why, you know, a backup can make a 53-man roster. Everybody's good. So, it's really us keeping the same mindset no matter who we're playing. We just got to continue to get better at our craft. >> Are there playing things in the games that you're not going to do? >> Uh we're going to continue to get our timing down. We're going to continue to get real game reps on mic points on protections, when I need to flip protections, when I need to when I need to reverse the call or make the make a whole new play call for myself if I want to check to something. Um but it is real game reps. Um but, you know, that's the beauty of it because we get a chance to we can have a a missed opportunity from my room, from the O-lineman room. We can have a missed block, the the backs can miss a cut. Um but it's all the little things that we're trying to get out of the way during the preseason so that way week one, you know, we can be on all 10. >> Talk about Bellinger since he's been here. What kind of addition he's been to this team? >> Uh he's great. Um the he he he knows his role. Um and I think what he's not going to get a lot of credit for is he's going to be able to help us a lot in the passing game. Uh he's able to break tackles. He's able to get key, you know, first downs on third and long, stuff that he did with the Giants. Um he's a great competitor. Uh he's a great teammate. He he shows up each and every day with the right mindset cuz it's hard to do what that guy does, you know, he's 260 maybe. He's blocking 330-lb people at his weight. So, you know, he he has the the right mindset each and every day. Um so, that that was a great addition, you know, that we added for sure. >> would you evaluate your mechanics, specifically your footwork through the first two preseason games? >> Uh I think it was good. Uh I think it's times, you know, I need to feel the the rush less um early in the game, especially if it hasn't made an impact. Um but as far as the timing of receivers, um I I believe we're at a we're at a great a great stop right now. Um it's not where we want. Uh we got some misplays, some missed opportunities in both games. Um but at the end of the day, it's about how can we avoid this come week one, um whether it's from my room, whether it's from the receiver room, um and it's all really, you know, playing the next play, cuz in the day we're going to have a a we're going to have a drop, we're going to have a bad throw, old line's going to give up a sack this year. Like, it's it's inevitable. So, you know, the more we can limit that stuff, the the more we'll be able to have a consistent and efficient offense. >> Josh Allen said that his advice to you going into year two would be trust the coordinator, working with the new coordinator. For you, like at what point did it get to where, okay, I fully trust Brian Daboll, and what was it that made you have that trust? >> Uh I trust him as soon as we hired him. you know, I had a great relationship, like I said, with him throughout the pre-draft process. Um but I could trust him from day one because he immediately took my my knowledge of the game, of what I like to run, what I was comfortable with running, and he immediately implemented in the offense. And so, that showed me right there that he's willing to at least listen to me. At the end of the day, he has a lot of stuff that goes through his head when he's calling plays. Um there's stuff that he has to protect, there's stuff where he can let loose and call whatever he wants. Um but he he knows that, you know, who he has as a quarterback, he knows I trust him, and he trusts me. >> Do you look at Caleb Williams, cuz there are similarities, obviously, in your game. Do you look at what he was able to do last year as something like, okay, that's something I can pull from in my year two? >> Uh yeah, we got a chance to watch their film uh a couple more teams' film as well. I think the the best thing about them that, you know, they were from his year to year two that they were way more efficient on first and second down. Um and that's really, you know, if you can keep yourself out of third and long, that's where you can potentially win a game. Um and that's why I think that we've grown already, you know, with Daboll here as the first year. Um myself, you know, the the whole offense, I think we've become way more efficient, you know, even in OTAs through training camp is being efficient on first and second down. Um and anytime we can stay out of third and long, you know, it's hard because in third and five or less, you pretty much know what they can play. They can still do something different. But when you get into, you know, third and six, third and, you know, seven, 10 plus, you know, that's when you got to really key in on your protections. Um it's going to be deeper drop backs. They know it's a drop back pass. So you're really playing, you know, at the defense's advantage. >> We're getting better every week. >> How would you How would Cam Ward assess the way Cam Ward has played so far this preseason? >> How would you assess it? >> Not well. >> You don't think so? >> I don't think so. >> I'm glad you don't think so. That's good. >> Cam, this is your >> How would you How would you assess it? >> You know, I assess it as, you know, did we win the game or did we lose the game? I assess it as what I can get better at. I don't assess it as um someone who can get up there and, you know, operate when the when everything's on. It's a It's a different process level. So it's more of, you know, slowing down the game to everybody. And I believe we made a huge jump from week one to week two because we're we're getting more condensed in the playbook. We're not really opening everything up. And you know, when we come to week one, I think it will hopefully it will be a different story. >> Cam, this is your third pre- third joint practice. This will be your third preseason game on Saturday. Have you added anything new to your process and and how you approach different things, how you approach your practices, how you approach, you know, your film study, and things of that nature now that you've had this time to mature into the offense? >> Uh I'll say consistently being in Coach Daboll's ear about what I like and then me consistently watching film with him and Shay, the quarterback coach. Um, cuz I I think we see the same things. Um, whether I'm in with the Mitch and the two, we're always thinking the same spot with the ball. Um, there was a couple situations today where I should have put the ball in different spots trying to force some things. Um, but I mean that's what, you know, I I have these practice these practices for because, you know, it's it's some it's some teams where you can you can you can fit balls into whole shots and down the middles. Um, just because whether the safeties get off the hash too much or whether they're not fast enough. So, uh, it's me consistently watching more on the the players I'm playing against and knowing what their, you know, strong suits are then, you know, what their weaknesses are then try to attack the weaknesses. >> You've been busy with camp, but have you peeked at the Jets a little bit as you get closer to week one or what what do you stand there? >> Uh, a little bit. Um, not too much though cuz we still got the Bears. Um, but I mean it's a we got, you know, two good defenses in, you know, this last preseason game and week one. Um, the the Jets they're going to be very physical. I got a chance to meet Coach Glennon in the pre-draft process. He's an awesome dude. Um, you know, the Bears are going to be a physical team. They play a lot of man coverage. They'll get to, you know, some some different zones as well. Um, so it's really about us, you know, taking our base plays that we're good at, going through our rules and then making good decisions. >> And what would you say is the the biggest thing the offense has taken away from facing three different defenses >> Uh, I think we took away that we're very physical. Uh, especially in the run game. I think the O line getting great movement. Um, then when we have to drop back, you know, we can do it at a successful rate. Um, it's really more of us doing it, you know, on first and second down um, so we can have a third and two or third and three so we don't have to be in a true drop back situation. Um, and I think the the best part where we are right now is our backs in protection. Uh, they they really you know, key in whether it's different fronts, whether it's easy fronts that our defense gives us at practice. Um, so I I think we're in the right direction. We just got got continue to keep going forward. >> Thanks, Tim. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Carnell Tate, Peter Skoronski & Jacob Martin After the Bears Joint Practice
text: out at practice. Then after practice, trying to stay consistent. >> How do you think it went today? >> Oh, it went it went pretty good. Um, we continue to build on our connection. We continue to get better as a team and as a program. >> What made today different? >> Uh, nothing made today different. I mean, I attack practice each and every day. Not every day is going to go your way. Just trusting the process. Uh, staying ready. >> It's kind of ups ups and downs of camp. How you feel like you've done that? >> I've done good. I think ups and downs comes with football. It comes with life. So you just got to get over those times. >> How did you come in knowing the ball to you a lot or was >> No, you never know. You know how you never know how practice going to go. You never know how the game's going to go. You just always got to be ready. And today the ball just found my came my way. >> How can you get the practices and the things that you're doing in practice to kind of translate over to the game? And is that more important to you uh in your process than maybe how you approach the games or have you approach the game? >> Uh you just got to stay you got to stay true to your process. Whatever you do throughout the week, Monday through Saturday to get ready for Sunday, you got to trust and believe that we putting in each and all the work through throughout that time period to go out there and perform our best on Sundays. >> Conversations like that after one day. >> Oh, we just hoping one. We're just hoping the best for one. Just uh just stand by his side and hoping everything goes well. >> You stay pretty even throughout this entire process. When you catch the first one today, do you feel like this is my day again? You kind of get back into that flow? >> Oh, no. It's just been football, bro. Like some days you going to have your day, some days not going to be your day. Just got to stay level at it. Uh just trust the process. >> What happened in the Seattle game on the one on the sideline? >> Oh, just just like I said, ballhead and hands. Got to come down with the ball. >> Greg Lewis, he talked about he would like to see you play with more violence. When you hear that, >> what how do you process that? How can you play with with more violence? >> I just playing a little bit more chippy than also just holding our line as a receiver when you running down the field. Just not uh just holding your line as straight as possible, not getting pushed to the side. was the first touchdown where you threw the corner on the ground example of playing more physical. >> Uh I mean you can look at it like that more physical. Yeah. >> Have you got where have you seen the most value out of the joint work with San Fran, Seattle, and now Chicago? >> I think I've seen the uh tons of looks. Uh I'm thankful for each and every team going out there against their ones, going out there against their entire defense, new defenses, seeing new things for the first time. So I think each each team has helped me in my process and getting better. How would you say you've progressed from day one in camp up until now as your receiver? >> I'm just getting more comfortable with the playbook and then just when I that allows me to go out there and play more fast >> the difference between playing at Ohio State and then seeing like you said these different defenses, different corners, and how you work your eyes, how you work your routes. How how have you adjusted with that to this point? >> Uh I've been adjusting pretty well. I mean, each team has helped me. Each team runs a different defense, different uh scheme. So, uh, getting exposed to that has helped me a lot seeing different coverages, how they rotate, some teams match, some teams doesn't. So, I think it all played a part then it just more complicated, more complex in college last week about the conversation you guys have against Seattle. How often do you have conversations like that happening about changing the routes, adjusting the way you guys play, that sort of there's conversations all the time, whether you did something good, whether you did something bad. I think as long as you you two are on the same page, that all that's all that matters. How close do you feel like you are to being on the same page right now? >> Uh, I think we're really close. Only time will tell. >> Growing up in Chicago mean anything to play these guys? >> Oh, yeah, definitely. Um, I I grew up a Chicago Bears fan. My dad's a Chicago Bears fan and still is, except when we play them. So, yeah, I'm just wishing this the city well. >> So, he's going to wear two blue. >> Not your guy. >> Uh, Jay Culla. We love We love Jay Culla out there. Matt Forte and B Marsh. All right. >> Did you get a chance to talk to Mandel before he went off? >> No, I didn't. >> Um, I guess they're not really consecutive, are they? I mean, they're a week apart, more than that even. Um, yeah, I think >> Indiana education. >> Yeah, whatever. You can't rely on those guys. Um, >> so I mean, I think it it's like just getting the good looks. Um, you know, getting different looks, seeing different fronts. um you know, you get kind of tired of, you know, beating up on your own guys, you know, so I think it's good to get go against other teams and almost get like a game-like atmosphere in a controlled environment um you know, for quarterbacks and and skill guys and stuff like that. So um you know, being able to go against three playoff teams, three divisional playoff teams, um and Super Bowl champions. So I think that's like, you know, it's hard to imagine a better word we could ask for in terms of quality and in terms of who came in here and who we went out against. So um yeah, I think they're hugely valuable. Um, you know, they're not always going to be perfect. They're going to be a little rough, but that's practice. That's training camp. So, um, definitely learned everything every week. I think >> Robert Sal said the energy and the feel of these joint practices, it resembles a regular season game more than the preseason games. And so, what do you think of that? You agree? >> I would agree. Yeah. I mean, obviously, you know, in these practices, you usually have everyone going that's healthy. Um, you know, preseason games sometimes you don't have, you know, guys out there, starters out there, etc. Um, so there is that there is definitely that energy um of the competition of being able to go against another team's ones um and really compete against them and like I said they control the environment but almost like kind of play out like a game too. So yeah, I do agree with that. I think there's there's a lot of chippiness, there's a lot of energy. You see the scuffles and stuff like that. Um it does feel like a game feels like a regular season game. So um having that experience and being able to do that against good teams is huge. >> It seems like there's a push like from the offensive line to not take any BS. Was that accurate or is that something that you guys were trying to Cuz you saw like Schlutman, he went right at uh you know, Woods after. >> Yeah, I was right behind. Um uh I Yeah, absolutely. Um you defend we defend our teammates, man. You know, we're we're going to stay within the whistles. Um you know, we're not I don't encourage throwing punches or fighting or anything like that, but you know, if cheap shots are taken on our guys, you know, it's unacceptable for us. Um you know, it starts with us, starts with our group, and you know, we're going to be there to defend our guys when they get it. Did you talk to Zav or what was your what was your vantage point of that hit on the line? >> Yeah, I just watched it again. It it looked, you know, pretty much that's on like teach tape one of one of terms of what not to do in a thud practice and a thud period. Um yeah, I think you saw me run down there. You saw Schlott run down there. Um that you can't have that, you know, you can't have guys like Wandell going down like that and hits that aren't necessary, you know, to I know I get we're being competitive. if they get, you know, DBs or physical stuff like that, but um that's like that's totally uncalled for in the practice setting like this. I think we're trying to take those out. Um you know, or else, you know, we could do things like cut guys or or clean out of the pocket or do stuff like that. You know, if you allow that, then okay, we can do that. So, um unacceptable and, you know, sorry that Wall had to had to go through with that. And yeah, >> Pete, you talked about that energy of the offensive line kind of defending teammates and having that in position of your will, right? Um, is that also something that you guys trickle down to the second and third units because those guys also seem pretty chippy and things go their way as well. >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. Um, it's a it's a room thing. I don't think there's just a starting five or second group or third group or anything. It's it's the room. It's our mentality as a group. Credit Karm and I think that's the mentality he's um promoted to us and it's, you know, he's kind of directed it. But then I think, you know, the first group starts, I think you always see JC in there and stuff like that. Um, but you know, even the rookies, you see Rasheed Miller in there. He's always like um you know it's it's our group mentality to protect our guys for sure. >> Tim said that something he's taken away from this preseason is that you have a very physical team especially running the ball. How have you seen that through the joint practices and preseason games from from an offensive line standpoint? >> Yeah, I I have seen it. I think it's heard in San Francisco. Um we had a lot we had some solid runs and just guys up front finishing. Um you know there's difference between having good games and like good physical gains and you see guys finishing gut blocks. you see guys straining. I think we saw that all three weeks against um you know each team we practice against um and and guys just continuing to sustain blocks and attack and then also running backs you know running with their pads low um you know not taking the thud, delivering the thud. Um credit to those guys too. I think you've seen that us do that kind of across the board across these past few weeks here. So um that's a really good thing. It's it's like I said it's one thing to get a good game. It's another thing to have a physically imposing game because the defense feels that and then now you got to line up again. They got to take on double teams. they got to tackle on the hole. Um so yeah, I'm proud of the group in terms of like being able to impose our will that way. Um that's a really good thing to carry into the season and kind of good thing to hang your hat on. >> What's it going to be like over these next couple of days closer to roster cut day? >> Um yeah, I mean it's always a a bit of a tough time of the year, I think. Um everyone everyone in this in this organization, all 90 guys have have worked their ass off so far. Um, obviously you can only keep 53, but um, that's professional football unfortunately and and you know, got to got to take the guys we got and and grow and you know, stuff changes throughout the year. So, you know, this isn't just the end all beall for everybody. But, um, yeah, it's kind of an unfortunate part of the year, but yeah, I think we're going to go out and compete Saturday and and leave it that way and kind of leave our mark as a group of 90, I think, is is a good way to go out and then what happens happens and we can, you know, shift our focus to New York. Imagine you probably got end up playing more in the preseason this year than you had in any other preseason going in. How much you think that'll help you? How much you think it'll be the off help the offense maybe be more crisp in week one? >> Yeah, I I do think that helps. It's good to feel the game. It's good to feel like a game and atmosphere and environment. As good as these reps are, you know, it's not at Nissan Stadium. It's not, you know, the same routine going in. Um so to feel that environment, doesn't matter who you're going against. um and have to execute in that environment I think is a really good to me it's like a mental thing just to feel what it feels like in a game on the sideline stuff like that um and to have that experience is huge I think we played in all three games and um to kind of feel like we have a lot of work and reps under our belt going into week one I think is is a huge advantage >> to work with Schlotty at center and then Carmona getting in more and more with you guys up front kind is like our like our north star a little bit like we he knows what he's doing he's on on the same page with Karma and the offense and Dave's um and we're very lucky to have someone to who knows this offense, knows the terms. It's a very high volume of terms in this offense and he knows him. Um and if you have a center who can get everybody right, uh that's that's a huge advantage as a line. It's a huge help as a line cuz um we're all learning it for the first time, but he's not. So really grateful to have him here. He's a great guy to work with, super tough, um super smart, and that's that's exactly the kind of guy you want to center. Um, obviously huge help to to Carmona and myself, but I think Fernando, like, you know, being a rookie, obviously he's kind of drinking through a fire hose a little bit. Um, but very impressed with the way he's just kind of attacked things and played physical. Um, you see him finishing guys, you know, dumping guys over piles. Um, just playing really hard. I think that's kind of the mentality you want in an offensive lineman and a young offensive lineman. Um, you know, he'll figure out all the other stuff that you only learn through experience. I think, you know, schematically just feel the game. But to see him take that mentality as a young guy and just kind of go full throttle and take it to guys, that's a great thing and I'm really proud of him that way. And he's he is learning and growing technically a ton. Um, you've seen it throughout camp. So, yeah, super impressive. >> Speak to the the shift in energy from that opening San Francisco joint practice to this joint practice today. Have you seen any growth of the team as a whole? uh and and if so, what things have changed for you guys in in two weeks or three weeks of time? >> Yeah, I think I really think I've seen consistency in terms of like perseverance of our energy. Um you know, it hasn't been like, you know, total dominance every single rep of every single joint practice we've had, but um you know, there's been es and flows of every single one of them. I think the group has continued to just work hard and persevere and find ways to make plays after bad plays. Um, and I think that's really what makes offenses great is the ability to like take the lows and then turn them into highs. And I think the group has done a really good job of that of okay, we start a little slow, okay, then we have some great completions in the team with the ball and then, you know, we have the big hit, you know, at the end of the two-minute and kind of feel deflated and then we go back and we score. So, like, you know, take taking those moments and there's been moments like that, you know, against Seattle, against San Fran, too. I think you've seen the consistency in terms of our um persistence and how we stuck with it and then that's a really good quality to have. >> You talk about how it's important just for you in the preseason relative to just kind of getting a feel for it and stuff just for the first team offense as a whole with it being the last opportunity to go out there and put something out there. How important is some type of consistency for however many snaps that you're there? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's it's really just about execution and and technique and being able to apply that the best we can. Like we understand we're not going to roll out the whole playbook here for a preseason game, but you know just executing the plays that are called and getting that right. Um you know it's not necessarily about results I feel like in the preseason. It's about process. It's about how we do it. It's about how we execute. Um and just and being on top of that as much as we can and understanding that it's all part of the process here at training camp. Um, and I think, you know, the more we can get the closer we can get to 100% in terms of assignment and fundamentals and those reps, I think is huge. And, um, [clears throat] just growing from that, but yeah, it's not always about like, oh my god, can we score 21 points in three drives? Like, obviously that'd be great, but it's really just about doing your job and just being executed at the highest level. >> What's the comfort? What's the comfort and confidence level you have in the guys next to you protecting Cam right now compared to this time last year? Yeah, I mean hard to say given given the different offenses and and kind of different room, but obviously great to have a, you know, Dan back next to me for another year. Um, I think our chemistry is continuing to grow. We have a really good feel for what we like like to do in certain scenarios and kind of, you know, how we treat things in certain ways. Um, that continuity is really good. It's really good to have a guy and tackle who you've been with. Um, and then having Shotty, I think it's been pretty seamless. Like I said, he's kind of like our our our brain in there and he's he's getting us all on the same page and so I think he's done a great job of having everyone work all together and I'm very like I said, I'm very grateful to have him here and and the help he's given us going forward. So very happy. Hard to compare, you know, year to year. It's just different guys and different schemes and, you know, different practice schedules. So um really just kind of in the here and now. >> Let me ask you on Bellinger just I know we probably do a lot of dirty work, but what have you thought about him and the teammate so far? how much you expect he's going to help help you guys this year. >> Yeah, super tough. You know, when the guys come over who are from New York that are here and all them speak super highly of him and how much they love him and know he's a quiet guy, but he's kind of in there throwing his body around, blocking on the edge. Um, you know, making catches when he needs to make catches and so that's kind of like the job description of a tight end and he kind of fits it to a tea. Um, you know, he holds up real well, I think, on the edge in terms of blocking. So, that's that's a really great asset to have. But um yeah, like I said, when when the guys who come over here all speak highly of him like that, it that's all the testimony you need, I think. [laughter] >> How things go from your perspective today? >> Shoot, man. >> Um I thought the D line came out with good energy. Thought we came out and uh you know uh showed our physical dominance and things like that up front. I think we handled the the things we need to handle um pretty well today. So, >> how has this camp been? Solid said that this has been one of the tougher camps that he's been around uh designed to be that uh how do you assess it? How has each of these sessions kind of been? He said it's like trying to play a quarter or game and a quarter uh to simulate that play. How have you seen it? this is it's been a great camp. You know, it has been physical. Um, you know, but the way the schedule's built out, it it allows you to get a full day recovery knowing that you got to come back out the next day and put every leave everything out there. Then you got a heavy lift after that practice and you got another 24 hours to recover and come back out here and do it again. Um, I think it allows you to uh maximize those days when you know you're in full pads and you know you're out here grinding. Um, it it allows you to not only recover properly rather than having, you know, four days straight of pads where you're where towards the end of the week things kind of you know, um it it allows you to to recover and come out here and put your best foot forward every day. Um and then that that that allows us to build that catalyst over time, you know. Um and we've seen it just in the joint practice when we have teams come out here u and practice against us. Uh you know, obviously the heat plays plays a part of it, but uh just how we structure and how we how we uh come in every day to attack the day, it clearly you can clearly see the difference in how we approach. For sure. I know you've seen most everything offenses can do in the league, but for some of these young players, what is the real value to see San Francisco's offense, Seattle's offense in this three very different offense this early? >> Um, I think it's super important. It allow it gives you perspective in terms of how teams see us and uh the things that they think they do well versus our front. Because like with us, things don't change much up front for us. You know, you know we're playing stud, you know where the DN's going to be, you know where the three techniques going to be, you know how we set the front. Um, so it it allows us to to play that mental game, right? We're going to see certain blocks from this group of coaches that have this like, you know, coach and tree family and we're going to see this group of blocks from this coach and tree family. Um, if you can compartmentalize it that way, uh, it allows you to play not only faster, but then you, okay, this team that does this, they push zone this way or they they slit blocks this way or the the why and you play differently on the edge and things like that. So, um, I think it's super beneficial to be able to see as many offenses as possible. >> For example, if the Bears tell you guys about yourselves, >> um, well, with Ben Johnson, you know, like they're going to they're going to run the ball, you know what I mean? They're going to run the ball. They're they have every run in the book. Um, you know, uh, traditionally or how you think about it in terms of like game breakdowns, right? um two runs that you that you think in second and long like traps and whams, like those get back on track type runs or even screens and draws um show up on second and long when they're behind when they're behind uh in their game plan. But with Ben Johnson's offense, you know, they can they'll screen on first down, they'll run a trap on first down, they'll run a wham, you know, on P and 10, they'll go crack toss, you know, off the jump, um play action off the jump. So it kind of it makes you have to play your rules true. Um, and if you can kill those problem plays and this front that's going to be, you know, any kind of like gap scheme, wham, pull, those are hard to hard to tell a dackle to run off the ball and then break down and go spill a wham or spill a trap. Um, but being able to to do that, you know, allows your guys to play a lot faster and I think the guys the D tackles today handled that for sure pretty good. >> How much has playing in the preseason helped you go into the season in the past? Uh, I value it, you know, uh, I know a lot of guys shy away from that, uh, getting into action early, but I think it allows you to get that pregame routine, even if you're in there for, you know, a quarter or half, you know, or even 10 plays. It allows you to get yourself in that that moment. It allows you to practice, okay, the buildup to a game. It allows you to practice, you know, how do I want to handle my pregame warm-up? How do I want to handle my preparation arriving to the stadium? I think it it's all it's all important to practice those things so when you come out to week one, you know, we're playing the Jets and you're not surprised by traffic or I'm surprised by, you know, um how we do our pregame warm-ups or how what's the timing wise. Um so I'm I'm big on on playing early in the preseason, whether it's, you know, 10 plays, 15 plays, a quarter, a half, whatever the case may be. >> Having success in the preseason, especially coming off a Sunday night, do you guys need to have a better showing on the Saturday? >> Um I think we're always looking to improve. you know, every time we step to step on the field, you're trying to trying to be better than your last performance, you know, uh uh everyone knows this, man, this business is about what have you done for me lately, you know? So, if you're if you're going out there and you're comfortable with what your last performance was, you're then you're not getting better and that's that's not that's not the way to to operate in the NFL for sure. >> Is there an energy shift from a joint practice to a preseason game? like that 24 hours in between those two events like you guys come out here and you're trying to impose your will trying to you know show something to another team but is that energy different than when you go into the game? >> Yeah, for sure. I think that's all part of it. I think the the energy is different from preseason joint practices to regular season to the playoffs, you know, all the there's always an energy shift in terms of urgency. Um and out here, you know, we're in a practice setting. Um so it feels a little bit more laid-back. You know, obviously like the intensity is similar, not the same, but similar. Um, and then when you get to the preseason game, obviously the intensity is up even a little bit more, the urgency is up even a little bit more. And then it it keeps it keeps compounding on itself as the season goes, you know, from the regular season to even November and December football to that playoff push to, you know, so on and so forth. >> And that building process, you mentioned it, Saul mentioned it. How much is it highlighted right now versus a year round thing, a careerlong thing? >> Um, well, I'm not I'm not I'm not sure which words you're asking. How much you guys talk about Bill Mallis getting ready for the season, the grueling parts of the year. Is that something you're working on year round, even in the before camp? >> Yeah, for sure. I think I think your your how you approach your off season shows up in training camp. You know, if you if you were excuse my language, sorry, I cuss a lot, y'all. uh as as as you were bsing, you know, through your offseason program, as you're as you ramp up through that OTAA period into training camp, you know, that shows. If you didn't if you didn't get your running in, if you didn't get your strength training in, that shows, you know what I mean? And now when you get to camp, now you're behind the eightball already and everyone else is already callousing their body for football, right? Because you the only way to get in football shape is to play football. Like you can run as much as you want. You can run hills, you can do bag drills, you can do all that stuff. But until you got, you know, 650 lbs on you, 300 lb on you that you got to push against, you know, play in and play out, that's the only way to get better at playing football is to play football. Um, but yeah, I think it's it plays a huge part in terms of callousing, right? Like you don't you don't think of callous as, oh, I'm doing this all year, you know, but for this eight months, I got to be locked in. I my ramp up has to be right. my recovery postseason has to be right so I can attack you know April, May, June, July up until August and then cool end of August. Now I should rather than you getting into end of September and you're hitting your mid-season stride, you're hitting your mid-season stride in terms of footwork, seeing the things you need to see earlier in the season. >> What's this next uh couple days going to be like for you? You guys played your last preseason game and a lot of these guys you shared the locker room with since camp are going to be leaving. What's that whole process like as as the team kind of whittleles down? Man, this is this is the toughest part of ball, man. You know, these guys have been here, you know, since March, April, um putting in that sweat equity uh to to make a team, you know, and uh unfortunately every obviously we can't keep everybody, you know, but there's 30 31 other teams in this league and your film is your resume, you know. So, as long as you continue to talk life into your younger players or to the guys that are on the bubble, you know that, okay, you may not be here, but I want to do well enough to where okay, I know I'm I'm making a 53 somewhere. You know what I mean? Um, it's always the toughest part of ball, man. And obviously the guys that are here, I'm excited to play with them. The guys that aren't here, man, I'm I appreciate their their their time, their effort. Um, and that brotherhood that that we built over over this past what, six months? I'm not sure. Six, five months. >> Last one. Anyway, >> appreciate it. Appreciate your time.

And uh talking for the first quarter of of both those games, we did not live up to a standard that I think we're kind of establishing here, especially when you watch us during the joints. But uh yeah, you'd like to go out there and finish strong. But is it going to make or break our season? It won't. >> Why is the joint practice more important than the game? >> Man, uh The These things right here are about as close to game-like as you can get. Um Something about those I you know, I don't want to speak for the player, but there's something about that game, those preseason games, you know, where they're Um I don't know. I don't know.
