I'm sorry. >> That down in the preseason games >> I don't know, you know, like from both sides you could, you know, but uh but at the same time like it's it's uh from a preseason standpoint, I'll be honest with you like there's a lot of things that you can learn from a game like we felt like we did. But at the same time the in You you could just feel like the intensity of these practices are about as close are probably closer to game-like than I would I would say that preseason game. >> Coach, I know you said you were initially going to talk to your guys about gradually maybe increasing the reps for guys in the preseason games. Is that still playing quick hard? Do you might apply to only be 20 25 plays or TBD? >> Um that's the plan. But again, that that is subject to change once I get in there and just see where our bodies are at. We've had a uh we've had a pretty extensive uh pretty difficult training camp. Like it's been heavy. Um every time we step on the field, you know, it's been a different model. So I I don't know if you guys have noticed, but every single one of our practices from a game look from a load standpoint has simulated a game plus a quarter. And so what these guys are walk after every practice, they're walking off feeling like they just played a game. And that was by design. And so we've had I want to say eight game-like practices, this including one of them. Uh so we're we'll see when we go in there how the what the rep count will be, but the goal is to get them through the first half. >> There have been some other coaches around the league referencing something that they presented to you guys, I think at the owners meetings, about what joint practice statistically with injuries meant relative to early season. Do you Does that ring a bell at all? it doesn't. >> Okay. >> Um I I do I do know that from a you know the I'll just speak candidly and this is my opinion, I'm not a doctor. So but um you know when with with sports science, you know, there you're either, you know, you're either injury prevention or you're sports performance. Um injury prevention, put bubble wrap on those guys, pat yourself on the back that you didn't have any injuries during training camp, but then you have a bunch of injuries during the first 4 weeks of the season cuz you're not calloused. And uh we've gone the other way to sports performance, to callous these guys as hard and as as well as we can, but at the same time being smart where we're actually relatively healthy. And um so there is a callous involved that I think the league is that sports science is forgetting, especially when you talk football because of the amount of contact and violence uh that happens with play after play and within practice. And uh so like I've said before, we're not even close to scratching the surface in terms of how to prepare a football player for the grueling part of the season. You know, like all the sports sports science has come from like soccer. You know, running yards and sprint yards, that's where it all evolved from. And uh we we hit we wear pads, like it's just different. And uh I think we're getting closer. I feel like we've had an outstanding training camp. I know this is our last one. And uh but the only way they're going to get better is if they see it. And as and they've got to see it a million times over uh if we want to accelerate the learning curve. Could you this is what I'm not happy with. Just go play football. It's technique. It's it's repetitive stuff like you you you're just you just want to see them work their technique, their fundamentals, their get-off, the cadence, the operation, going through a 2-minute drive, going in the red zone, going in short yardage, getting all the different like all that stuff matters. Um and you just want them to just be exposed to football. So, the be exposed to four different schemes uh like that to me is priceless. And then offensive or defensively, you know, you got Day ball scheme, which is different than Kyle's scheme, which Seattle's not different, but we needed to see it cuz a lot of teams do it. And then uh Ben Johnson's scheme is different. So, getting all getting all the exposure, you learn you learn schematically what you need to make changes to. You you learn a lot about yourself one from a competitive standpoint. That that part's easy. But from a schematic standpoint, you learn a lot with regards to how you need what little tweaks and changes you need to make within your scheme to prepare yourself for week one. >> This is the last time you guys walk off the field with 91 players out there. What's the message you give to the guys about >> the work they've done up to this point and for the guys who are fighting to be part of the 53? >> Um I I I I really appreciate this group, you know, like it's our it's our first group. Uh appreciative of the work that they've all put in like and and a lot of guys uh and I'm thankful for this. They fought There's a lot of guys who fought through a lot of injuries. They're all fighting for jobs and they've made themselves available. They've fought through pain. Uh they've been attentive. They've been doing everything we've asked them to do and uh and I and I hope that their experience is one that they all feel like they've gotten a little bit better. >> If you'll pardon the out-of-towner question, Caleb Williams has got a skill set that's pretty unique. What was the benefit to your defense to being able to go against >> Hell yeah. I I'm a huge fan of Caleb. You know, like there's no there is no lead safe with Caleb. He's an unbelievable quarterback. He's elite off schedule. Uh he can play he can do it all and the amount of growth he's had in the last year and a half has been amazing and uh credit to the coaching staff and all the things they do with him, but uh he's a stud in every way. >> At what point does training camp truly turn into focusing on week one? >> Monday. >> All right.

title: Dave Ziegler on Roster Cuts, the Waiver Wire & the Rookie Class | Press Conference
text: Um, excited about today. You know, another great opportunity for us as an organization to compete against a team like Chicago Bears. Team that was in the playoffs last year. Um, great opportunity to evaluate our guys matched up against some different players and I'd say between Chicago, Seattle, and San Francisco, um, just been an awesome opportunity for us to to to compete against um, some high-level teams and to evaluate our guys and you know, busy time in the scouting world right now. Um, you know, we're in the the uh, roster evaluation cut down, evaluating the league period, um, of uh, of our operation and we're continuing to work through that and um, you know, obviously that will conclude over the next couple days and we'll be ready to roll and so on to the Jets after that. So, uh, that's what I have. I'll open it up for questions from you all. >> Go ahead, Teresa. >> At this point, that's the thing. Uh, you know, you've got you're trying to get this board set for the final 53 cut on Sunday. Looking around the rest of the league for guys who might come off the waiver wire. Is I mean, is this literally the busiest time of the season this week or does it ramp up as you go into Sunday? >> No, I think this is this is the busiest time, you know, and and probably one of the busier times of the year. You have so much more, I'd say certainty in free agency in the draft cuz you know those players are available. And so, right now it's a lot of, you know, looking at rosters, how many, you know, how many players have teams capped at certain positions, what's their philosophy, what guys could come available, what guys not cuz you have to be efficient during this time, too, and not spin your wheels on a bunch of players that are going to make the team. And so, um, yeah, we're cramming uh, every day, every opportunity we have. We're in the, you know, on our film room going through films. We're talking to all 31 teams, getting an idea of where they stand, what they're looking for, um, seeing if there's anything that match and I just working through that process. >> What's the waiting process or the philosophy maybe on keeping experienced players versus keeping developmental players at the bottom of the roster. >> Yeah, I think it you know, it's position by position. Um, and I think you you know, you just you're you're kind of measuring, right? Where that um, younger player is in their developmental phase, what that gap is between them and the veteran player. Um, and so I think that's part of the equation. And then now with the elevations, that goes on to the practice squad now. You know, where where on the practice squad may we might need a more experienced player that can come up and elevate and play in a game versus maybe a position where we feel like we have experience and we can you know, have a developmental player that we can work with and bring along during the course of the season. >> What do you make of the depth you guys have at offensive line right now? Is that a potential position you're looking at from the other 31 teams? >> Yeah, a lot of young guys, right? And and a lot of guys that I think have done really well for themselves here during camp. I I think they've showed out not only in practice but in in the joint practices going against other players. And I think when you've watched our games, I think you know, we've been pretty especially running the football like those guys have done a good job working together. But offensive line every every single position, you know, our job is to evaluate the roster and find ways to improve it, right? Every position, every role. The players' jobs here like they're all here be for a reason. We want them to be here. Their job every day in practice, joint practice, preseason games, meeting rooms is to prove to us that that they belong here and that they're not going to find anybody better. And so, you know, the offensive line in that regard will be no different than any other position. If we can find a way to improve it and and that opportunity presents itself then that's what we'll do. >> You're supposed to be efficient in like an evaluation process. How does having tape in-house with three different teams that you guys have joint practices with help with that? >> Yeah, you get to do a deeper dive, you know, and and and it is really helpful because that's the tough thing about preseason tape. Like, you're evaluating a guy maybe off 40 snaps. And so, for these joint practices and the teams that we've competed against, being able to look at all the different periods where they competed against us, it just it expands that, you know, expands that play count and it just gives you more evidence, you know, in your evaluation. >> It may be different in each case, but do you think the biggest factor is now [clears throat] or maybe not who's the fourth best running back, but it's the fourth best running back rather than the sixth best best receiver? Is that kind of what you're working through a lot of these spots? >> Yeah, there's those conversations too, cuz you want to keep the best 53, but as you know, there's also a certain amount of players that you have to take to the game at each position to be able to operate on Sunday. And so, yeah, but you're looking at that, you know, just like you said it, you know, is there is the is the fifth fifth or sixth corner, you know, is that of more valuable for us as we get into the season than the fourth or fifth back? And those are tough conversations and but those are things that we have to work through. >> What's the kind of realistic range of the number of players now for this team and spots that are still number of spots that are still up for grabs in the last few days? >> Oh, man. I It would be tough for me to It'd be tough for me to put a specific number on it, but I would say, you know, there are you know, there's there's a handful of jobs that are still up for grabs that we're going to evaluate. That's a big week for some guys here in this joint practice and in the game. And then we'll see where it shakes out. >> Building the practice squad, how much of that is involved as well in pairing down the 53, trying to see who you can keep, scouting other rosters to to fill that, and having the flexibility of having up to six players with unlimited experience, does that make it easier these days? >> I think that it does depending on kind of what your roster construction looks like. And so, you know, if you feel like you're inexperienced at a lot of different positions, you can get to six quick, you know, and so I think you have to be a you know, strategic again as I mentioned earlier of what you have on the roster and what you feel you know, what the relative experience is to performing on Sunday at a high level and if you feel like hey, we really need to offset this with a veteran guy at this position then then you have to do that. But the elevations you know, do give you some advantages of really like you have your 53 but then you have you know, these all these you know, all the practice squad guys that you can bring up and it gives you just more flexibility. >> What is your assessment of this rookie class maybe through these joint practices and the two preseason games? >> Yeah, really excited about the rookie class. I think they've all continued to grow. They've all continued to improve as they get more experience. The thing about not only the rookies but the second year players that I think a lot of times you know, we all fail to realize is there's so many new things that they get exposed to in a joint practice or in a preseason game that they've never seen before. And so it's an opportunity for them to download a new you know, some new information, learn, apply it to their skill set and get better and I think we've seen that with each one of our our rookie players here that we drafted and and our second year players are continuing to go through that process. >> Maybe maybe Femi in particular as the just doing new scheme and staff. >> Yeah, I like this scheme fit for him. You know, Robert talks about it fast and violent and I think you know, Femi can get off the ball fast. He's a violent player. You know, he he he plays with extreme effort and those three things fit very well into very well into Robert's system and and Femi still a guy that as we know played off the ball for a period of time at UCLA. Getting on the ball was new for him last year and in odd front some different responsibilities within that you know, that position in the odd front and now he's going so there's there's definitely it's you know some adjustment for him, but I think like I said fast physical violent high effort, you know, he has all those attributes. >> He doesn't really watch the whole lot of preseason games and scouts and everything, but you guys give him a project and that's how you go about. Do you guys do that for all coaches and how do you go about forming that that project for them to to evaluate? >> Yeah, we do is is where is Mike had mentioned I think in you know his opening press conference. We're setting a board very similar to the way we set a draft board together. Now, the categories are a little bit different cuz they're not rounds. You have you know you guys that you would consider claiming guys that you would consider adding to the practice squad. There's another category of guys that you would you know that you would work out. And so as we kind of whittle that list down here's the guys we would claim or consider claiming. Here's the guys that we're going to be available. Give those guys off to the coaches have them evaluate them come together and make sure we get on the same page with those players. >> A couple more guys conversation about the team and how you know filling needs and whatever. How much do you know do you get or how much does everyone I guess know in that world before the 5:00 deadline hits on Sunday as far as what's going to be out there? >> I'd say you have a pretty good idea. I'd say you know it gets to the point where especially now this week where teams are really starting to kind of hone in on what who they're going to keep who may you know who may be on the roster bubble. You're having more direct conversations on specific players on other teams rosters that you know are going to be you know are going to be available.
